findings.title: A halt's paused project folders are unpaused by the next sequencer stop()/pause() (tray Quit, self-upgrade, Resolve-exit restart, tray Pause, drive unplugged)
findings.what: halt_all_sync stops the sequencer and then pauses every lane C folder. Sequencer.stop() and pause() both end in _unpause_all(self._last_selection), which checks neither _is_halted() nor the halt latch. Every later stop()/pause() in the same process therefore releases every selected project's Syncthing folder while the halt is still active. A restart with a persisted halt never re-pauses them. CR-48 fixed this for the shared folders and the release path, not for project folders going through stop/pause.
findings.failure_scenario: A fleet halt is active. The editor quits the tray, a pushed update restarts it, the editor quits Resolve (so _maybe_recover_stale_bridge restarts the companion), the editor clicks Pause, or the SSD is unplugged. Any of these calls sequencer.stop()/pause() and unpauses every project folder. Syncthing then syncs project files both ways during the halt while the tray and the grid still say STOPPED. Probe output: pause calls during shutdown while halted: [('s-a', False), ('s-b', False)].

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. halt_all_sync (app.py:7631) first calls _stop_lanes, which calls sequencer.stop(). It then pauses every folder in halt_folder_ids via _pause_lane_c_folders(True). But Sequencer.stop() and pause() (sequencer.py:733-758) both end in an unconditional _unpause_all(self._last_selection). _last_selection is kept after a stop, and _unpause_all (1785) filters only on item validity, upload_only and unconfirmed ignores. It never checks _is_halted(), and _is_halted() is only consulted at 2190, inside the pass loop.

Every later path in the same process therefore releases the selected project folders while the halt is still active:
- shutdown() calls _stop_lanes() unconditionally (around line 10705), so tray Quit and the self-upgrade hand-off both reach sequencer.stop().
- toggle_pause (9245) calls sequencer.pause() in managed mode with no halt check.
- _root_pause_lanes (2890) calls sequencer.pause().

Syncthing runs as its own service (the docstring of _pause_lane_c_folders says so), so the unpaused folders really do sync while the halt is on.

On restart the halt is re-read from disk. The _start_lanes HALT gate returns before sequencer.start(), so _startup_unpause never runs, and nothing re-pauses the folders either. note_fleet_flag returns None for a fleet halt that is already active, so halt_all_sync is not re-run. The only calls to _pause_lane_c_folders(True) are inside halt_all_sync. release_for_halt/CR-48 only covers the release path.

Nothing in CLAUDE.md or KNOWN_BUGS.md makes this intended or already tracked.

Impact: a fleet or local halt, the "stop touching the files" safety stop, is silently broken for project folders by an ordinary Quit, update or Pause, while the tray and the grid still say STOPPED. Severity high stands.

findings.title: Consolidate ignores the halt, the licence gate and the sign-in gate, and runs lane A upload and lane B rclone sync directly
findings.what: consolidate_project checks sync_enabled, the tray pause, config_problems and the root, but not _lanes_refusal(). It does not check halt, EULA or _login_gate_blocks_sync. RcloneLane.run_once has no halt check, and its stop event is never set on lanes that never started.
findings.failure_scenario: The companion restarted with a persisted fleet halt, or with the licence unaccepted, or not signed in. The editor runs 'Copy this project's media in'. Originals upload to the NAS and a delete-capable rclone sync pulls proxies during the halt. When the halt was engaged mid-run instead, both runs return early and the toast still says 'Copy & upload finished'.

findings.title: An admin's diagnostics request is marked answered before the upload, so a failed upload is never retried
findings.what: _apply_diagnostics_request writes applied_request=requested_at to diagnostics_sent.json before starting the async upload, and the upload's result is discarded. The dashboard keeps the command standing until a bundle arrives, and every redelivery is refused by the persisted stamp.
findings.failure_scenario: The admin clicks [ ASK THIS MACHINE WHY ] on a machine with a flaky uplink. The 256 KB POST fails (timeout, 5xx, 413, or the identity lapsed). The machine never uploads, and the dashboard shows 'diagnostics requested' forever until the admin clicks again.

findings.title: The pending-relink 'done' answer can never land: the dashboard only updates rows with applied_at IS NULL
findings.what: The RES-10 re-answer (ok=True, relink_pending cleared) is sent after the move row was already stamped applied by the first relink_pending=True answer. mark_file_move_applied matches only applied_at IS NULL, so it updates 0 rows. The companion has already cleared its ledger flag and never answers again.
findings.failure_scenario: A move lands while another project is open, and the relink later succeeds. file_move_targets.relink_pending stays 1 forever and the relink detail never arrives. Nothing renders the count today, which is why this is low.

findings.title: An off-cycle report runs _on_report_response concurrently with the reporter thread's own
findings.what: resume_lane_b, called from inside _on_report_response on the reporter thread, starts a second post_once on a new thread. Its reply fans out through _on_report_response concurrently with the first. The diagnostics stamp, file_moves entry->apply_move and _resolve_undo_answers are check-then-act with no lock.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin clicks RESUME on a tripped machine that also has a redelivered file move or diagnostics ask. Both threads apply the same move or upload two bundles.

findings.title: _queue_file_move_answer appends outside the lock res-companion-5 added
findings.what: Only the filter-assign is under _file_move_answers_lock. The append runs after the with-block, so the reporter's swap can take the list before the append lands (the answer is lost), and concurrent queuers for the same id can both append it.
findings.failure_scenario: The watcher's _relink_pending_moves queues its answer as the reporter drains. The answer is dropped and never re-sent, because the ledger was already cleared.

findings.title: The posix single-instance pid file never checks that the live pid is a companion
findings.what: On macOS the guard is companion.pid plus os.kill(pid, 0), and the file is never removed at shutdown. After a reboot or crash, the recorded pid can belong to an unrelated live process, and the companion refuses to start.
findings.failure_scenario: After a Mac reboot, the old pid belongs to a system daemon. The LaunchAgent start shows 'CCSync is already running' and exits, and the machine has no companion until someone notices.

findings.title: A blocked repath is finished on the next pass by pointing Syncthing at the directory that lane B or the structure clone created
findings.what: When the move fails, the folder is left paused, but _process_project still runs the structure clone and lane B for the project's NEW rel. Both of those create local_root/Projects/<new rel>, and lane B fills its Proxy dirs. On the next pass, _move_dir sees a live source and an existing destination and takes the 'conflict, re-point anyway' branch (returns True). Reconcile then re-points the folder at the proxy-only directory, unpauses it, and records a false 'moved your copy' event.
findings.failure_scenario: The admin renames 2026/Old to 2026/New while the editor has the project open in Resolve. Pass 1: the move fails and the project is marked blocked, and lane B pulls proxies into New. Pass 2: the Syncthing folder is re-pointed at New and unpaused. New holds proxies only: no .stfolder and no lane-C assets. The real project stays at Old, outside every lane's scope, so lane A stops uploading its originals. The blocked sentence is replaced by a false 'CC Sync moved your copy'. Resolve is relinked to paths that do not exist. The probe reproduced this with a fake admin.

verification.reason: The mechanism holds at HEAD. repath.reconcile (repath.py ~432-455) records a blocked event when _move_dir fails and leaves the folder paused. But sequencer._process_project (2045-2067) does not check the blocked state before continuing. It goes on to _maybe_clone_structure(subpath) (on the first pass, when every<=1, or when the N-pass age is due) and to _run_lanes_a_and_b for the NEW subpath. Lane B mirrors proxies into local_root/Projects/<new rel>, and the clone mkdirs the skeleton there. On the next pass, reconcile sees actual (the old path) != expected. _move_dir finds src.is_dir() True and dst.exists() True, and takes the 'target already exists ... re-pointing the folder anyway' branch, which returns True (repath.py 564-569). Reconcile then calls set_folder_path(expected), records moved_note (a false 'moved your copy'), relinks Resolve old->new, and calls set_folder_paused(False) directly, with no .stignore or .stfolder check. The blocked branch's own comment names this exact hazard: 'the structure clone then creates it -- so Syncthing sees the whole project's lane-C set as deleted' (AUDIT_2 DEL-5/L-8). The conflict branch reintroduces it one pass later. KNOWN_BUGS SYNC-10 only covers reporting the orphaned old tree after a genuine stale-copy conflict. It does not cover this blocked->lane-B->conflict path, and no open entry covers it. Real effects: the Syncthing folder is unpaused and re-pointed at a proxy-only directory with no .stignore and no .stfolder. At best Syncthing errors on the missing marker. At worst it treats lane C's set as deleted. The real project at Old sits outside every lane. The blocked sentence is replaced by a false success note, and Resolve is relinked to paths that do not exist. High stands.

findings.title: Server-followed moves on small passes stay on the breaker's cumulative counter and trip 'slow leak'
findings.what: note_pass calls relocation_probe only when the pass would trip or trashed at least 25 files. The relocations _relocate_trashed already knows about (_moved_out_of_trash, _server_relocated_keys) are therefore never discounted on smaller passes. The later discount is clamped to the current pass's deletions, so it cannot take back relocations from earlier passes.
findings.failure_scenario: Ten passes each follow 20 hand-moved proxies to their new folder, and deletes climbs to 200. The next pass that trashes 2 genuinely deleted proxies trips BREAKER_CAUSE_LEAK with 202 files and parks lane B until a human resumes it. The probe reproduced this.

findings.title: The disk-floor park keeps a stale sentence and never clears after the trash prune frees space
findings.what: The park clears only at 2x the floor (40 GB), but the disk-pressure prune stops at 1x the floor (20 GB). The prune can therefore never produce the self-release. While parked, check() keeps returning the reason built at park time, so the free-space figure the editor sees is stale.
findings.failure_scenario: A laptop parks at 10 GB free with 30 GB of trash. The prune frees space up to about 22 GB and stops. Lane B stays parked indefinitely, and the tray and fleet chip still say 'this drive has 10 GB free, and proxy download needs 20 GB'. Only a manual RESUME helps. The probe showed check(25 GB) returning the 10 GB sentence.

findings.title: The stray-project scan and express attribution compare disk paths to dashboard rels without NFC folding
findings.what: _refresh_stray_projects and _project_rel_for_path compare names read from os.walk or watchdog with the dashboard's NFC rels using only normcase/lower, unlike every other comparison in the file, which goes through nfc_key (CR-90).
findings.failure_scenario: On a Mac with NFD names, a selected project such as 'Matej Šimalčík' is reported as a stray 'in no sync plan' along with its bytes. Express never attributes its new clips, so they wait for the rotation.

findings.title: A file lane B moves to the trash counts as 'transferred' as well as deleted
findings.what: 'Moved into backup dir' matches the 'Moved' branch, which increments transferred before deleted is incremented.
findings.failure_scenario: A trash-only pass of 12 files shows 'transferred 12 file(s)'. _last_run_moved counts each file twice. Feeding the tally the measured record pair gave transferred=1, deleted=1.

findings.title: A proxy that cannot follow turns a completed move into a failed one, and the retry drops the relink
findings.what: apply_move wraps src.replace(dest) and move_proxy_siblings in one try, so an OSError from a proxy returns (False, 'could not move it') after the original already moved. The row becomes retryable, not applying, so the retry's resume arm does not trust it and answers (True, 'nothing at the old path on this machine', None).
findings.failure_scenario: Windows editor with Resolve in proxy playback holds the proxy open; admin moves the clip. Attempt 1 moves the original, the proxy raises WinError 32, and the toast says the copy did not follow. Attempt 2 returns ok with paths=None, so no Resolve relink runs and relink_pending is False: the clip stays Media Offline and the proxy is orphaned under the old Proxy/. Probe: attempt1 False/orig at new True; attempt2 True 'nothing at the old path', proxy left behind True.
findings.ledger: new (companion twin of the dashboard-side two-phase fix, KNOWN_BUGS ~6745)

findings.title: An upload-only borrower still builds a borrowed lender, so the tray tells the editor to ask an admin who cannot fix it
findings.what: _build_borrowed skips invalid items but not upload-only ones, so an upload-only borrower's includes go into _borrowed_lenders. The dashboard shares a lender folder only for FULL borrower ticks, so no offer ever arrives and BorrowedFolderManager records not-offered permanently.
findings.failure_scenario: A borrower ticked upload-only gets the permanent line 'Lender has not been shared with this computer yet. Ask your admin to approve it.' in the lane C detail and report, and the admin has nothing to approve. If the lender folder already exists locally from an earlier full tick, it stays restricted-but-unpaused and keeps pulling the borrowed subtree down on a no-download tick. Probe: lenders={'lender': {...,'borrowers':['borrower']}} for an upload_only borrower.

findings.title: A full borrower whose lender is ticked upload-only never receives the borrowed subtree (both sides)
findings.what: Both sides decide 'the lender's own runs cover this subtree' from the selection without its mode. The dashboard marks covered when the lender is in fetch_selections rows of every mode. The companion drops the include when it sits under any rel in rel_to_slug, which includes upload-only rels, and treats a lender in slug_to_item as selected. An upload-only lender runs lane A only, so nothing brings the subtree down. This breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every reader deciding what comes DOWN must filter to FULL.
findings.failure_scenario: A laptop ticks Borrower (full) and Lender (upload-only, to back up its originals). Borrower's borrowed Lender/Interviewees never arrives: no lane B proxies, no lane C files, no borrowed folder, and no problem sentence anywhere. Probe case 2: includes={} lenders={}.

findings.title: A sequencer thread that outlives stop() can unpause a folder after the halt paused it
findings.what: halt_all_sync runs sequencer.stop() first (5 s idle wait, then a 10 s join) and pauses lane C folders only afterwards. _verify_current_folder_unpaused runs right after _wait_for_folder_sync returns on stop, with no stop check, and accept_folder ends in an unconditional set_folder_paused(False). One wait iteration can take 15 s or more, and set_ignores has a 30 s timeout, so the join can time out while the thread is still inside one of these calls.
findings.failure_scenario: A fleet halt is pressed while a slow Syncthing or dashboard has the sequencer mid-call. stop() returns, the halt pauses every folder, and then the old thread sees the current folder 'still paused after its lane C turn' and PATCHes it back to running (or accept_folder unpauses a new folder). That folder syncs through the whole halt while the tray says nothing is sharing.

findings.title: Borrowed-folder negations are escaped with a backslash, which Syncthing on Windows reads as a path separator
findings.what: escape_ignore_glob puts a backslash before [ ] { } * ?. Syncthing's documentation says escaping is not supported on Windows because the backslash is the path separator, yet [ ] { } are legal in Windows file names. A negation for 'Interviews [raw]' is therefore parsed as 'Interviews /[raw/]'.
findings.failure_scenario: On a Windows editor, a borrowed subtree whose name contains brackets or braces matches no negation, the trailing ** ignores the whole lender, and the subtree never arrives. The Mac, which honours the backslash, works. No problem is reported because the restricted list reads back exactly as written.

findings.title: The cached plan is not keyed by editor, so a sign-in as someone else can run the previous person's projects
findings.what: selection.json stores {fetched_at, response} without the editor, and nothing clears it on sign-out. get() falls back to it whenever fetch() returns None, including when there is no identity yet and when the new editor's fetch fails. _startup_unpause also reads it. The in-memory TTL is keyed by editor; the disk fallback is not.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor A signs out and B signs in while the dashboard is restarting, or B's first fetch returns 401. The sequencer then runs A's plan from the cache: lane A uploads and lane B downloads A's projects on B's session until a live fetch succeeds.

findings.title: Re-pointing a shared asset folder does not move its contents or create the path and marker, yet reports 'repaired'
findings.what: When the folder's path differs from the wanted path, _reconcile_one PATCHes the new path onto the running folder with no pause, no mkdir guard, no mkdir and no move. Syncthing creates a root and .stfolder only for newly added folders, so the re-pointed folder comes up in 'folder path missing' or 'folder marker missing'. The 'repaired' outcome clears the FolderProblems entry, and the CR-278 heal skips the folder because the marker is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: After a local_root change (canonical_prefix or tree_name change, or a Mac volume remounted under a new name), the LUT library is pointed at an empty, non-existent path and stays in error indefinitely. No tray line, lane detail or report field shows it, because lane C only judges selected folders.

findings.title: Ingest file picker builds a Tk root outside _popup_active_lock, and its timeout abandons a live dialog whose answer is dropped
findings.what: _tk_pick neither takes nor checks app._popup_active_lock, so on Windows it builds a second live Tk root on a loopback helper thread beside the fixer/Settings/update dialogs (the CORE-M3/H8 sibling-root hazard every other site locks against; apply_upgrade's locked() guard does not see it). pick_media_sources times out after 300 s and answers 'cancelled' but never closes the dialog; a later pick lands in a box nobody reads. On macOS the modal picker stays on the main thread after the timeout, so the docstring's promise not to park the dispatcher is false.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor opens 'Choose from this computer', returns after >5 min and picks a folder: the page already said cancelled, the pick is silently dropped, and a second click opens a second picker beside the first (two roots on two threads); or the watcher's fixer popup opens while the picker is up.

findings.title: macOS: async menu rebuild landing while the menu is open drops its weak delegate, leaving ui_state.menu_open set forever
findings.what: icon.menu assignment only enqueues _apply_menu_now on the main queue; if the menu opens between enqueue and execution, the block runs during tracking, rebinds self._delegate/_targets and releases the old watcher. NSMenu.delegate is weak, so menuDidClose_ never fires and menu_open is never cleared; the refresh/pulse loops skip forever while it is set, and resolve_bridge waits up to 8 s before every call.
findings.failure_scenario: Mac editor right-clicks the menu bar icon just after a lane state change: after closing the menu, the icon colour/tooltip/menu never update again this session and every Resolve call is delayed 8 s; items clicked in the stale menu do nothing.

findings.title: WorkProgressWindow.close() before the root exists reports closed, then the window opens anyway, untracked
findings.what: close() with self.root None sets _closed and returns, so _close_work_window's wait_closed succeeds and the app forgets the window, but the thread then builds and shows it; a close between tk.Tk() and run_dialog fails the cross-thread after() and likewise leaves it up.
findings.failure_scenario: A b-roll batch auto-opens the ingest window and the editor immediately opens the proxy window (or shutdown starts): the ingest window appears after being 'closed', a second live root that close_work_window/shutdown never closes or waits for.

findings.title: Work-progress window is a Tk root outside _popup_active_lock
findings.what: app.py says the work window is one-at-a-time because two live Tk roots is CORE-M3's wedge, but it only serialises against other work windows; it auto-opens on batch start without touching _popup_active_lock, so it coexists with the fixer/Settings/update dialogs and apply_upgrade's locked() guard ignores it.
findings.failure_scenario: A b-roll batch starts while the out-of-tree fixer popup is up: two roots built and pumped on sibling threads at once.

findings.title: Five tray.py dialog builders abandon a mapped root when widget construction raises (comp-ui-6 shape fixed only in Settings)
findings.what: _build_sign_in_dialog, _build_typed_confirmation, _build_credentials_dialog, _build_update_dialog and _build_scripting_warning_dialog build tk.Tk() then widgets with no destroy on the exception path; comp-ui-6 showed this leaves a frozen, uncloseable, permanently pinned window, and fixed it for settings_window/PopupDialog only.
findings.failure_scenario: An RDP reconnect/display change while the typed REMOTE/DELETE ANYWAY confirmation is being built leaves a frozen half-built window on screen; the lock is released and every retry adds another.

findings.title: _WindowsIcon._teardown iterates _hicon_cache unguarded while loops may insert; a raise skips _stopped.set()
findings.what: A pulse/refresh tick already past its _ccsync_stop check can insert into _hicon_cache via _icon_handle while the pump thread iterates .values() in _teardown; the RuntimeError escapes run()'s finally before self._stopped.set().
findings.failure_scenario: Quit or self-upgrade during a colour change while pulsing: stop() waits its full 5 s and a spurious crash report is written for an ordinary Quit.

findings.title: An admin's undo sent during Resolve's launch window is recorded FAILED and never retried
findings.what: apply_undo classifies the bridge's refusal by substring. STARTING_MESSAGE ("DaVinci Resolve is starting up") matches none of PARK_HINTS/RETRY_HINTS and has no 'not', so it returns 'failed'. The other three disconnection messages all return 'retrying'.
findings.failure_scenario: The dashboard undo command arrives while Resolve is in its CR-68 launch window. The pool walk answers STARTING_MESSAGE, the ledger records the undo as failed and the command is retired, so the wrong clip paths stay in place. Verified with a snippet over DISCONNECTION_MESSAGES.

findings.title: The 20 s project-name cache files a relink under the PREVIOUS project, which brings back the cross-project undo hazard
findings.what: current_project_name() caches the name for 20 s and nothing clears it on a project change. _before_mutation, the automatic relink rate limiters and the adjacent-proxy journal entry all read it. After a switch, the save point exports the old project by name, journal entries go under the old project's slug, and the old project's allowance is spent.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor switches from A to B within 20 s of any cache refresh, and the unprompted canon relink rewrites B's clips. The journal says project A. Undo in B refuses and says to open A; in A the project check passes and B's entries are replayed against A's clips on shared Assets paths, unjournalled. That is the comp-resolve-2 outcome again. Snippet confirmed the name stays 'A' after the switch.

findings.title: Cards sweep_items runs the API walk under _API_LOCK when no library is available, throws the result away, and speeds up the watcher's full-walk valve
findings.what: get_timeline_items(allow_cached=True) falls back to _get_timeline_items_locked when the library walk returns None. sweep_items then rejects the 'api' items after the walk has already held the lock. Every cached hit also bumps the shared _polls_since_full_walk counter, so the full per-clip walk runs about every 7-8 s instead of about 30 s.
findings.failure_scenario: With cards_agent on and no readable library (or 60 s after any library error), each 1 s engine sweep costs a lock-held track walk plus the engine's own walk, and a full walk of up to 11 s lands every ~8 s. The tray, watcher and card clicks starve behind it. Snippet: sweep_items returned None after one API walk ran.

findings.title: Restarting the Cards role after ONE loop dies leaves the other loop running on the released engine
findings.what: supervise_now restarts as soon as any loop dies. _clear_dead calls engine.stop() and starts a new engine and client, but the surviving daemon loop of the old client keeps calling role.call, which serves any caller without a generation check.
findings.failure_scenario: The push loop dies and the watchdog starts engine #2. The old pull loop keeps taking /cards/agent/pending commands and applying them through the stopped engine #1, which shares the same bridge. Two engines then drive one Resolve with synthetic keystrokes, the breach the role exists to prevent.

findings.title: On macOS the CR-68 probe spawns lsof while holding _API_LOCK
findings.what: connect() calls script_server.state() inside _bridge_call. On Darwin that is an lsof subprocess (5 s timeout), re-run every 250 ms when the cache expires. The module's own rule says no subprocess may run with the bridge lock held.
findings.failure_scenario: On a Mac a slow lsof blocks the watcher, pool refresh, b-roll insert and Cards sweep behind _API_LOCK for the length of the spawn, several times a second while Cards is on.

findings.title: An SMB blip at the reservation re-check leaves the original 0-byte reservation orphaned for good
findings.what: When the reservation stat raises OSError, a fresh name is claimed, but the original empty reservation is neither removed nor tracked. No tmp is left beside it, so sweep_orphan_reservations can never find it.
findings.failure_scenario: A stat blip at the end of a FIX ALL copy leaves a 0-byte clip.braw next to clip (2).braw. Lane A uploads it, --ignore-existing makes it permanent, and lane C fans it out fleet-wide (the COMP-GUARD-1 outcome).

findings.title: The uid-map cache is keyed on `project is <cached object>`, which a fresh GetCurrentProject() wrapper probably never satisfies
findings.what: Every lookup reconnects and calls GetCurrentProject() again. If fusionscript returns a new proxy object each time, the identity test never passes and every uid lookup and every 100-clip enrichment chunk walks the whole pool again.
findings.failure_scenario: FIX ALL over 50 clips does 50 full pool walks under _API_LOCK, and a 1,300-clip enrichment does 13 walks instead of one. The tests pass because their fakes return a single object.

findings.title: The library finds the project by name only, so a same-named project in another folder supplies the pool
findings.what: _find_project_id takes rows[0] of a query by ProjectName. Resolve allows the same name in different folders, so pool_items and changed() can read another project's media pool.
findings.failure_scenario: With two 'Interviews' projects, the pool walk returns the wrong project's clips. Proxy relink and classification plan ops on uids that are not in the open pool, so every op fails as not-in-pool and the real clips are never considered.

findings.title: LUT adoption leaves `<name>.ccsync-tmp` behind on a failed copy
findings.what: copy_into_library writes to a fixed tmp name and never removes it when copy2 or os.replace raises.
findings.failure_scenario: A full disk or locked destination during Adopt leaves a partial .cube.ccsync-tmp in the shared LUT library for good.

findings.title: A batch holding two clips with the same name indexes the first clip twice and never the second
findings.what: The claim manifest carries no local_id, so the companion pairs manifest rows with staged files by (orig_name, rel_dir) and takes the first match. Two staged items with the same name and rel_dir both resolve to the first item's local_path, while each row keeps its own hash.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor drops card A's C0001.MP4, then card B's C0001.MP4 (the page appends drops into one batch, no name dedupe) and runs the batch. Card A's bytes are proxied, described and uploaded as both C0001 and C0001_2 (the second row carrying B's hash). Card B is never indexed, and its staged copy is later pruned. Nothing reports a failure. Probe1 confirmed this: both rows came back with local_path S/i1.mp4.

verification.reason: The mechanism holds end to end. The page never removes duplicate names. ingestAddItems (ingest.js:438-463) appends each drop to ing.items. ingestCollect strips a single dropped folder's name from rel_dir, so two Sony/Canon cards dropped one after the other both produce the same rel_dir (for example PRIVATE/M4ROOT/CLIP/C0001.MP4). prepare stages every item under its own local_id path (broll_ingest.py:1551). create_batch (ingest_batches.py:569) stores orig_name and rel_dir per item, and the claim manifest carries no local_id. _item_from_manifest (broll_ingest.py:1891-1901) pairs rows with staged files by (name, rel_dir) and breaks on the first match, so both rows get item 1's local_path. The only other check is line 2292, where item["hash"] = item.get("hash") or self._hash_fn(source). That keeps the manifest hash (card B's) and never checks the file bytes against it, so nothing fails. _allocate gives the second row a _2 name, and card A's footage is indexed and uploaded under both slots. KNOWN_BUGS.md has no entry for this, and nothing in CLAUDE.md makes it intended. _staging_holding uses the same name+rel_dir key and has the same blind spot. The result is silent wrong content in the archive, and a clip the editor believes was ingested never is. Severity stays high.

findings.title: keep sub-folders unticked, or a folder name safe_name rewrites, fails every sub-folder clip with 'not on this computer any more'
findings.what: The server blanks rel_dir when keep_subfolders is off. Otherwise it rewrites each component through safe_name. The staging entry keeps the raw rel_dir, so the exact string compare finds no candidate, local_path is empty and _crunch_item fails the item. retry-failed repeats the same failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A folder drop Shoot/Day1/*.MP4 with keep sub-folders unticked, or a folder named 'Day 1.': every clip fails at the first stage with 'the source file is not on this computer any more', even though the files are sitting in staging. Probe1 confirmed this: 'Day1' vs '' and 'Shoot A.' vs 'Shoot A' both matched nothing.

findings.title: Insert's download-done branch is unreachable: finished fetch jobs leak, and the stand-in row is never rewritten before import
findings.what: rclone renames the file into place before the job is marked DONE, and each re-POST checks is_file() first, so the fetch block is skipped. As a result the DONE job is never popped. A stand-in is imported while its ledger row is still a sizeless intent (the 'BEFORE the import' rewrite with size/pending_fetch/upgrade never runs). A later re-insert after the file is gone reads the stale DONE, answers 'file not found ... is the share mounted?' and, for a stand-in, forgets the row.
findings.failure_scenario: After a stand-in insert, probe3 showed the row as {size: None, pending_fetch: True, upgrade: None}. With no geometry and a companion restart before settle_intents runs, job_state is None for ever, so is_standin stays True even after the real original arrives. Probe2 showed a deleted clip re-sent failing once with a misleading 'is the share mounted?' while the registry still held a 'done' job.

findings.title: Staging held after one original failure is held for ever, and the disk-full message names a button that cannot free it
findings.what: _note_original_failed adds the clip to held_for_base_rig, and nothing ever removes it: not when retry-failed later uploads the original, and not when the rerun batch finishes (_note_staging_ended returns early because ended_at is set). Held entries are skipped by both the retention sweep and CLEAR FINISHED STAGING. staging_report still counts them as finished bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: In a 150 GB drop, one clip's original fails 4 times; the editor retries and it succeeds. The whole 150 GB stays in .ingest permanently. When the disk fills, the next drop is refused with a message telling the editor to use CLEAR FINISHED STAGING, which removes nothing.

findings.title: Ingest encodes have a fixed 15-minute ceiling, so long clips on CPU-only machines lose their proxy or the whole item
findings.what: The preview and editing-proxy encodes run under run_ffmpeg's flat 900 s timeout. A timeout becomes rc 1, reported as 'did not decode'. proxy_gen runs the same own_proxy_cmd with ceiling max(1800 s, duration x 60) because long encodes legitimately take longer.
findings.failure_scenario: A Mac or AMD machine (CPU pass only) ingests a 25-minute 4K clip. libx265 10-bit at about 20 fps needs about 30 minutes. Both passes are killed at 15 minutes, so the clip loses its editing proxy. With a slow enough source the preview fails too and the item is failed.

findings.title: Upload queue survives a normally finished batch, carrying its paused state and done/failed ledger into the next batch
findings.what: Only cancel and lease-lost drop _uploader. _maybe_finish does not, contrary to _new_queue's once-per-batch docstring. On the next run() the old queue's _done/_failed rels remain. A paused queue is never resumed, because run() sets _upload_paused from the claim and the heartbeat then compares against the already-updated flag.
findings.failure_scenario: On retry-failed of the same batch, a stale failure for the original's rel burns an upload attempt before any rclone runs. If the queue was paused when the previous batch ended, the next batch's uploads never start and its items sit in 'uploading' while the lease is heartbeated.

findings.title: A conversion longer than 120 s leaves the pre-conversion original eligible for lane A and the Resolve importer under its final name
findings.what: The executor converts in place beside the finished original, and the original is not written again while ffmpeg runs. 120 s after it lands it passes lane A's --min-age gate and the importer's settle test. The YT-3 --no-mtime fix only closes the case of a conversion shorter than 120 s, and the work-file excludes never cover the original under its final name.
findings.failure_scenario: A 10-minute 1080p clip arrives as VP9 and the libx264 re-encode takes 10+ minutes. Lane A uploads the VP9 file under the final name, and --ignore-existing keeps that undecodable copy on the NAS for good (/ytdl/fetch then hands it to other editors). youtube_import files the VP9 original into Master/Youtube. Resolve then holds the file open, swap_in falls back to '.converted [id].mp4', and the result is two clips per download.
findings.ledger: related to YT-3 (partly fixed; its recorded fix does not close its own symptom)

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. How it happens:

- **Download location.** `_download_one` downloads into `destination_for(...)`, which is the canonical in-tree `<project>/Youtube/<term>` folder. Lane A carries `Youtube/` up on purpose (`build_filter_rules_up` has no Youtube exclude, and `build_filter_rules_down`'s docstring says requester-first clips reach the NAS through lane A).
- **Conversion.** `_ensure_edit_ready` (ytdl_executor.py ~2512-2551) writes `<stem>.editready.mp4` beside the finished original `<stem> [id].mp4`. While ffmpeg runs (the timeout allows hours), nothing writes to the original again. `--no-mtime` stamps it with the moment it landed, so after 120 s it passes lane A's `--min-age 120s` (rclone_lane.py:1739).
- **Lane A filter.** `YTDL_WORK_EXCLUDE_RULES` excludes only `*.editready.*`, `*.original.*`, `*.temp.*`, `*.fNNN*.*` and `*.failed`. The original under its final name is not excluded.
- **No coordination.** Nothing connects the executor to lane A or the importer: there is no in-flight exclude path and no pause. The only `exclude_paths` caller is the express lane.
- **Importer.** youtube_import.py:667 settles on age of 120 s or more plus an unchanged size and mtime. A file that is not being written passes that on its second scan.

The fix record is incomplete. KNOWN_BUGS YT-3 is marked "PARTLY FIXED" and notes that "the staging option (download outside the tree) is still open". Even so, it claims that `--no-mtime` makes `--min-age` "a real gate again". That is only true for conversions shorter than 120 s.

Conversion is common in practice. `prefer_avc` avoids re-encoding at 1080p and below when YouTube offers AVC. Above 1080p (1440p and 4K rungs, VP9/AV1 only) a libx264 re-encode routinely takes more than 2 minutes.

Two impacts are permanent or visible:

1. **Undecodable copy on the NAS.** `--ignore-existing` keeps the pre-conversion bytes on the NAS for good under the final name, and other editors are handed that copy.
2. **Two clips in Resolve.** The importer puts the VP9 original into the media pool. Resolve then holds it open, so swap_in's `os.replace` fails. It then renames the original aside to `.original` and places the converted file under the final name. The Resolve clip now points at the `.original` file. The finding says the fallback goes to `.converted [id].mp4` instead; that detail is slightly off, but it only changes which duplicate you end up with.

The base rig is not affected because it writes straight onto the NAS. Every editor machine that downloads above 1080p is.

findings.title: Stop, quit or lease loss during 'converting' leaves the unconverted original as a finished clip
findings.what: When _should_stop() fires during the ffmpeg re-encode, the tmp file is deleted but the VP9/opus original stays under '<title> [id].mp4'. It is not disowned, because _cleanup_current only clears sweepable names, so the importer, lane A and the dedupe scan all treat it as the deliverable.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor presses [ STOP ] (or quits the tray) while the tray says 'converting to H.264'. The undecodable original stays in the project, the importer files it and lane A uploads it. If it reaches the NAS first, the server's [id] disk dedupe marks the clip a duplicate and never converts it. Probe: the folder afterwards held only the original bytes and only 'downloading' was posted.

findings.title: A mid-job 403 (sign-out, expired or revoked identity) never stops the executor; it downloads the whole job unrecorded while the server re-downloads it
findings.what: Only a 410 ends a local job. heartbeat() discards the status and clip_status swallows non-200. require_fleet_caller answers 403 before _leaseholder_or_410 can answer 410, so a machine whose identity token is gone keeps downloading every clip while the lease lapses and the server reclaims the job. A 404 is ignored the same way.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor signs out, or the 30-day token expires, mid-way through a 40-clip job. The machine fetches all 40 clips from its residential IP and posts 40 refused statuses, while the NAS downloads the same 40. The progress mirror shows the job finished locally.

findings.title: One failed yt-dlp install or floor update switches local downloads off for 24 hours; nothing retries sooner
findings.what: The sidecar loop is the only effective caller of ensure(). After an ACTION_FAILED pass it publishes ok=False and sleeps CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS (24 h); the 15-minute recheck applies only while the feature is off. The executor's poke cannot fire, because capabilities() refuses before any claim. The ffmpeg/deno sidecar pass has the same 24 h retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A new machine's first ensure(), 30 s after login, runs before Wi-Fi or a captive portal lets it reach GitHub. The install fails and the machine has no local downloads until tomorrow. Likewise, one GitHub blip during '-U' after an operator raises the floor sends every affected machine's jobs to the server for a day.

findings.title: swap_in's last-resort deliverable is the sweepable .editready temp name
findings.what: When all three renames fail, swap_in returns tmp.name ('<stem>.editready.mp4') as the delivered name and it is posted as filepath_rel. That name matches _INTERMEDIATE_STEM_RE, so a later clear_partials for the id deletes it, the importer ignores it, and the dedupe scan cannot see it. In the non-same branch the original may already be deleted.
findings.failure_scenario: An AV scanner holds the files during the swap, the clip is ledgered done at a .editready path, and the next attempt at that id sweeps it away. The ledger then points at nothing.
findings.ledger: related to YT-6 (fixed; branch not covered)

findings.title: A crash-loop revert does not stop the machine re-installing the build it just fled
findings.what: revert_to_previous_build records the bad version only as reverted_from. It is never a failed attempt, and no gate reads it: _upgrade_attempt_blocked, auto-update and the pushed-update path check only attempts/backoff, and the dashboard's _upgrade_info keeps offering and pushing the same version.
findings.failure_scenario: With auto_update on or an admin push, vX crash-loops and is reverted to vX-1. The restored build's first report brings the vX offer/push back and it reinstalls vX at once. In round two the supervisor has used 2 of its 3 relaunches for the hour, so it refuses after one more. vX then has only 2 starts, crash_loop never trips, and the machine has no companion until the next logon, after which the cycle repeats.

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. revert_to_previous_build (upgrade.py:1012-1019) resets last_version.json and calls note_reverted_from, which only sets reverted_from/reverted_at/reverted_announced. Nothing in companion/src reads reverted_from as a gate. The only uses are the toast (app.py:11022), the report payload (app.py:7055, 8817) and _note_report_accepted, which clears the marker after the first accepted report (app.py:6660-6665).

_upgrade_attempt_blocked (app.py:6671) checks only upgrade_attempts_exhausted and upgrade_retry_due. When vX started successfully, the ledger load (app.py:~6648) called clear_upgrade_attempts because record.version == VERSION. So after the revert, vX-1 sees attempts 0 and no last_attempt_at, and retry is due.

Auto path: _on_upgrade_available -> compare_to_running says vX is NEWER -> _maybe_auto_update. It passes the blocked check, the offer matches, and apply_upgrade runs.

Push path: _upgrade_attempt_blocked is the same gate. On the dashboard, _upgrade_info (api.py:5772) offers the channel's current or targeted build with no machine_state.upgrade_reverted_from check. That field is only used in soak/alerts (db.py:4602, alerts.py:1800). The push command at api.py:9816 is re-emitted while the request stands. If vX crashed before ever reporting, the push is not cleared by _update_push_done.

The reinstall creates a fresh .old and start record, so the crash loop can re-arm. The supervisor's relaunch cap (3 per hour, persisted in state/supervisor.json, per KNOWN_BUGS) makes the second round end with no companion, as described. Otherwise the machine ping-pongs.

No KNOWN_BUGS entry treats this as intended. APP-5/REL-8 describe the revert as terminal ("standing down"), and nothing re-offers-guards it.

It needs a crash-looping release plus auto_update (off in the vendor build) or a pending admin push. That is exactly the scenario the revert exists for, and it defeats the revert and can leave the machine without sync. High stands.

findings.title: APP-5 rollback copy is deleted seconds after start, so the crash-loop revert cannot fire on an online machine
findings.what: keep_old_exe_until_healthy treats one accepted report as health. The first report goes out 2 s after start and the keeper checks before its first 30 s wait, so <exe>.old is deleted within about 2-32 s. That is shorter than the 60 s timer APP-5 replaced, and revert_to_previous_build then finds no rollback copy.
findings.failure_scenario: APP-5's own scenario: a build reports once, then dies 3 minutes in. It is relaunched and dies 3 times in 10 minutes, so crash_loop is true, but .old was deleted at about 30 s. The log reads 'did NOT roll back: there is no rollback copy', so a fleet-wide bad build is only revertible on machines whose dashboard is down.

verification.reason:
The mechanism is real. In app.py:11073-11078 the keeper runs with `self._report_accepted.is_set`. keep_old_exe_until_healthy (upgrade.py:927-944) checks healthy() before its first 30 s wait. The reporter posts its first report after INITIAL_DELAY_SECONDS = 2.0 (reporter.py:101), and _note_report_accepted (app.py:6655) sets the event. So on a machine that can reach the dashboard, `<exe>.old` is deleted about 2-32 s after start. That is sooner than the 60 s timer APP-5 replaced.

APP-5's own symptom in KNOWN_BUGS.md:5180 is "starts fine, puts a tray icon up, and hits a fault three minutes later". An online machine reports before that fault, so .old is already gone. When crash_loop later becomes true (3 starts in 10 min), revert_to_previous_build (upgrade.py:986-987) returns "there is no rollback copy". The auto-revert only works where the build dies before its first report, or where the dashboard is unreachable. The guard does nothing in its headline scenario on the normal fleet.

This is not refuted: KNOWN_BUGS APP-5 and RESILIENCE_SWEEP row 14 say "keep .old until the first accepted report" on purpose. But that choice is the defect, since it contradicts the symptom the entry was written to fix. No open entry covers it.

Why I downgraded it from high:
(1) Manual recovery still works. A crashing build still reports within seconds of each start. CLAUDE.md makes republishing an older build a first-class rollback, and `commands.upgrade` / `auto_update` push it. So a fleet-wide bad build can be recovered by the vendor without touching each machine.
(2) Nothing is corrupted or lost. The effect is the loss of an automatic safety net, and the machine has no tray until the rollback is pushed.
(3) The crash loop itself only builds up through the supervisor (at most 3 relaunches an hour) or through logons, so the auto-revert was a narrow net to begin with.

findings.title: Site manifest (feature flags, smb_unc, sftp tuning) refreshed once per process start
findings.what: refresh_site runs once, on a background thread at start, and never again. If that fetch fails (a machine that starts before Tailscale is up), there is no refresh at all this run. feature_enabled reads only the cache, so a site change lands only after a tray restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner turns youtube_download OFF (the legal off switch) and running companions keep serving ytdl for days. Turning auto_update ON has no effect until each tray restarts. A machine that started offline keeps a stale smb_unc for the grade swap.

findings.title: Sign-in /verify path carries no arch and no upgrade_none_reason: offers a wrong-CPU build and clears a standing refusal
findings.what: The report path sends arch and receives upgrade_none_reason. verify_credentials sends neither and forwards only 'upgrade'. VerifyIn declares no arch, so _upgrade_info offers every arch. app.sign_in feeds {'upgrade': X|None} to note_report_response, which clears the refusal when there is no offer and no reason.
findings.failure_scenario: An Intel Mac signs in while current is arm64: the tray offers it, and with auto_update on it is applied, the exec fails, it rolls back and an attempt is counted (REL-16's symptom). A machine refusing a retracted build signs in: the refusal is cleared, and later reports carry upgrade_none_reason, which does not restore it, so the REFUSING chip and the alert vanish for good.
findings.ledger: related to REL-16 and comp-app-3 (fixed on report path only)

findings.title: Manifest scan that overlaps a drive unplug reports zero files for the remaining projects
findings.what: refresh_once checks root presence only BEFORE a walk that can take minutes. os.walk (no onerror) swallows scandir errors and size_fn OSErrors are skipped, so a drive that vanishes mid-walk yields 0-file rollups that replace the cache.
findings.failure_scenario: A Mac editor ejects the SSD mid-refresh. The cache and the next heavy report show 0 originals/proxies for most projects, so the dashboard presence view shows the editor holding nothing, which is exactly the 'indistinguishable from deleted' state the pre-check exists to prevent.

findings.title: Repaired machine id not reported until the tray restarts, although the toast says 'from the next check in'
findings.what: DashboardReporter caches an empty machine_id for the process lifetime. machine.remint() (the Settings repair) never invalidates that cache.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor presses GIVE IT A NEW ID and is told it will be reported at the next check-in. Every report keeps sending machine_id null until restart, and a rename in between still loses the plan-carry affordance.

findings.title: Sign-in with an unusable reply token overwrites a working identity.json
findings.what: save_identity() persists the new token before self.valid() is checked. On failure, only the in-memory identity is reset.
findings.failure_scenario: A signed-in editor re-signs in, and the dashboard returns a token this build cannot parse. The tray reports failure, but on the next start the broken file loads as invalid: the machine is signed out and, with require_login on, stops reporting.

findings.title: Media jobs and proxy generation spawn the bare name 'ffmpeg', so a machine whose only ffmpeg is the managed sidecar copy advertises the capability and fails every encode
findings.what: ffmpeg_available/_resolve_binary fall back to the sidecar-installed ffmpeg when the bare default is not on PATH, and capabilities report ffmpeg+ffprobe true from that probe, but jobs_media and proxy_gen put the unresolved config value ('ffmpeg') in argv[0]; Popen only searches PATH. ffprobe resolves (ffprobe_for), ffmpeg never does. music_clap_sidecar and ytdl_executor resolve first; these two do not.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor laptop with only the vendor-installed managed ffmpeg: reports ffmpeg:true, is offered proxy-480p/audio-extract/peaks, claims, fails in ~1 s with 'could not start ffmpeg: [WinError 2]' (retryable), earns the 120 s cooldown, job tours the fleet. proxy_gen on the same machine gates RUNNING and fails/caps every clip with the same spawn error; remote editors never get proxies.

verification.reason:
The finding holds on every point I checked. In ffmpeg_tools.py, ffmpeg_available() (lines ~187-224) and _resolve_binary() (~128-139) fall back to sidecar_tools.managed_path('ffmpeg') when the bare 'ffmpeg' is not on PATH. capabilities._ffmpeg and _ffprobe therefore report true on a machine whose only ffmpeg is the managed one. KNOWN_BUGS confirms this was intended: the 0.7.9 note says "capabilities() turns ok the moment ffmpeg lands", and CR-53 says every vendor-build machine fetches the pinned ffmpeg-static unless it already has one.

The spawn paths never resolve the name. jobs_runner.py:1167 passes str(cfg.get('ffmpeg_path','ffmpeg')) into MediaJob. jobs_media's audio_copy_cmd, audio_opus_cmd, proxy_cmd and peaks_cmd put str(ffmpeg_path) at argv[0], and _run_ffmpeg Popens that argv. proxy_gen.py:558 stores the raw config value. own_proxy_cmd, preview_proxy_cmd and verify_decodes_cmd (ffmpeg_tools:909 returns [ffmpeg_path, ...]) put it at argv[0] unresolved, and proxy_gen:326 runs subprocess.Popen(cmd). Nothing in the companion adds the tools dir to os.environ['PATH'] (grep found no PATH mutation). So a bare 'ffmpeg' spawn raises FileNotFoundError / WinError 2 whenever PATH has no ffmpeg.

The code treats ffprobe and ffmpeg differently. ffprobe goes through ffprobe_for, which calls _resolve_binary and returns the managed sibling. music_clap_sidecar:778/810 and ytdl_executor:1742/3141 both call _resolve_binary. jobs_media and proxy_gen are the only callers that skip it.

There is no guard and no open KNOWN_BUGS entry for this. Net effect: a laptop with only the managed ffmpeg advertises ffmpeg and ffprobe, claims proxy-480p, audio-extract and peaks jobs, and fails each one on spawn. proxy_gen passes its availability gate (same fallback) and then fails every encode. That is the default setup for a vendor-build editor with no ffmpeg of their own, so high severity stands.

findings.title: Companion job gate ignores the dashboard's per-kind idle floor (60 s for audio-extract/peaks) and the base-rig exemption
findings.what: The scheduler offers cheap kinds after 60 s idle and exempts base-mode machines from the idle floor (ranking the base rig first for cheap kinds), but the claimant applies one flat jobs_idle_seconds (300) to every kind and has no base-mode exemption, so it sits at STATE_USER_ACTIVE and never claims. The offer carries no kind, so the gate cannot choose a floor.
findings.failure_scenario: Base rig with Alex at it (or no console session, idle None): dashboard offers a peaks job and /why calls it eligible and first-ranked; the companion refuses indefinitely, the 60 s grace expires, the lane waits on another machine. Laptops idle 60-300 s never take cheap jobs, so the 60 s decision never takes effect.

findings.title: out_stem is used as a filename unvalidated: absolute stems write anywhere, '/' or ':' in a multicam name land in the wrong place
findings.what: job_paths.resolve refuses absolute and climbing rel_paths, but the stem is appended after with no check: Path(out_dir)/'C:/x' discards out_dir, '..' climbs, '/' makes an uncreated subdirectory, ':' on NTFS makes an alternate data stream.
findings.failure_scenario: out_stem 'C:/Windows/Temp/evil' writes C:\Windows\Temp\evil.peaks on the claimant. Multicam name 'Interview 1/2' makes the .partial open fail (dir not created) as a retryable failure touring the fleet; 'Q&A: Ruskin' on Windows writes an ADS of file 'Q&A' invisible to the page.

findings.title: Peaks job on a clip with no audio is a retryable failure, so it tours the fleet cooling every machine down before it pins
findings.what: _peaks probes audio but discards the codec, runs ffmpeg, which exits non-zero ('Output file does not contain any stream'); the code != 0 branch raises MediaJobError with default retryable=True. The non-retryable 'no audio to draw' branch is reachable only on exit 0. _audio treats the same condition as non-retryable.
findings.failure_scenario: Cards queues peaks for a video-only angle; each machine fails it retryably and gets the 120 s job cooldown until the retry budget is spent and it pins to the dashboard engine, which fails again; every visited machine was unavailable for real work and blamed for the failure.

findings.title: Proxy generator gate checks ffmpeg but not ffprobe; with no ffprobe every clip fails and is capped while the state reads RUNNING
findings.what: capabilities treats ffprobe as its own capability, but proxy_gen's gate only asks ffmpeg_available. A missing ffprobe makes probe_video raise UnreadableMediaError for every clip, recorded as a failure of the clip.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor with a lone ffmpeg.exe on PATH (so the sidecar installs nothing): gate says RUNNING, every queued clip fails 3 times and is capped until restart, history fills with 'ffprobe could not be run', gap never closes, nothing says install ffprobe.

findings.title: Music insert at playhead fails whenever a clip straddles the playhead on the target track (ripple moves it into the new cue)
findings.what: affected = items with GetEnd() > rec includes a clip starting before the playhead; it is re-appended whole at start+shift, which lies inside the new cue's span [rec, rec+shift). Per place()'s own note Resolve refuses occupied spans, so the verify raises 'ripple failed' and the insert rolls back (or, if Resolve overwrites, the cue tail is destroyed). Re-appended clips also lose volume/fades/effects.
findings.failure_scenario: Playhead parked mid music bed on A2, editor presses insert on A2: 'insert failed; rolled back N/N clip(s) on A2' every time, with no hint to razor the bed or use place underneath.

findings.title: Music ingest decode holds ~3x the track's PCM in the tray process, and tracks over 2 h get a false 7200 s duration
findings.what: communicate() holds full f32 stdout (N), nan_to_num allocates N, .copy() another N: ~690 MB per audio hour, ~2 GB peak for a 1 h mix, ~4 GB for 2 h, in the sync companion. '-t 7200' truncates the decode and duration is taken from the decoded sample count.
findings.failure_scenario: 90-minute mix on an 8 GB laptop: ~3 GB allocation in the tray during decode (MemoryError or heavy paging with Resolve open). A 2.5 h DJ set is recorded as 2:00:00, skewing the duration-based duplicate defence.

findings.title: Job input rejected by Path (NUL byte) escapes _execute_media/_execute_whisper uncaught; no result posted, every machine silently drops the job
findings.what: Handlers catch only JobPathError; Path.resolve/stat raise plain ValueError('embedded null character'), which propagates out of tick() to a log line. No result is posted.
findings.failure_scenario: rel_path with a NUL: claimed, dropped with no result, re-offered after the 300 s lease expires, dropped by the next machine, each one taking the lease-expiry cooldown as a machine that went quiet mid-job.

findings.title: The scheduler only ever looks at the first 200 queued jobs, so a block of jobs nobody can run starves every job behind it
findings.where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:10255 (queued_jobs limit=200), used by db.py:10534 claim_next_job and jobs.py:931 offer
findings.what: Both the offer builder and the claim CAS walk only the top 200 queued rows by priority DESC, id ASC. Queued jobs never age out, a job nobody can run never spends its retry budget, and whisper never pins. So 200 or more jobs nobody can run hold the window closed, and nothing behind them is ever offered or claimed.
findings.failure_scenario: 250 whisper jobs (GPU required) sit queued while the GPU box is off, then peaks/audio-extract jobs are queued. Every report refuses the 200 whisper rows and never sees the cheap jobs. The base rig is never offered them, and explain() calls them schedulable. Probe: with 200 whisper jobs plus 1 peaks job, queued_jobs has no peaks row, and claim_next_job returns None even with allowed_ids=[peaks_id].

findings.title: A project with more than 2,000 proxies shows the extra proxies as downloads owed for ever, and the note says the total may be too low
findings.what: The lane B backlog is NAS proxies with no matching editor_media row. The companion lists at most 2,000 proxies per project (and sets truncated), so every NAS proxy past that counts as missing even though it is on disk. The template renders manifest_truncated as 'totals may undercount', but for downloads the total is too high. CR-314 fixed only the case where originals plus proxies together pass 2,000.
findings.failure_scenario: The NAS holds 2,500 proxies and the machine holds all of them. Its manifest lists 2,000 with truncated=True. fetch_sync_backlog returns 'down 500 files' for good, the same phantom queue CR-314 was filed for, and the note says the count may be too low. Probe output: down 500 5000 True.

findings.title: Forgetting a computer or a person leaves their diagnostics bundles behind
findings.where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:8435-8439 (_MACHINE_STATE_TABLES) and db.py:1114 (diagnostics table uses editor/machine columns)
findings.what: forget_machine and forget_editor delete from _MACHINE_STATE_TABLES, which does not include diagnostics (its columns are named editor/machine, not editor_username). Up to five 256 KB bundles per machine stay for up to 30 days.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin deletes a departed editor. Their diagnostics text (paths, hostnames, logs) is still readable through fetch_diagnostics, and a new user given the same username inherits the old bundles.

findings.title: Approving a second computer's SSH key erases the first computer's key on the NAS
findings.what: approve_pending_ssh_key installs the offered key via nas.create_or_update_editor(username, key_text, None), and both NAS backends REPLACE the account's key: TrueNAS PUTs sshpubkey as that single key, and Synology overwrites authorized_keys with `>` + `mv -f`. Local mode appends, so only the shipped NAS modes are affected. There is no guard for a key that differs from the existing one.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor with a working computer (K1 on the NAS) runs the wizard on a second computer. onboard._offer_ssh_key posts K2 and the admin clicks approve. The NAS now holds only K2, and computer 1's lane A upload and lane B proxy download start failing SFTP auth, with no warning shown at approve time.

findings.title: File move that renames leaves the proxy under the old name; a same-folder rename reports PARTIAL falsely
findings.what: FileMoveIn.to_path can rename, and undo relies on that, but _move_proxy_siblings always targets dest.parent/Proxy/<old proxy name>. A same-folder rename finds its own proxy 'already at the destination', so the move is stored partial and the route answers 207. A rename into another folder keeps the old stem, which breaks Resolve's Proxy/<stem> auto-link. For a case-only rename the companion DOES rename its local proxy to dest.stem, so the NAS and the editor's disk disagree and lane B downloads one proxy and trashes the other.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin renames A/A001.mov to A/Renamed.mov. The original is renamed, the proxy stays Proxy/A001.mov, the move shows PARTIAL 'something is already at the destination', and every machine loses the proxy link. Probe: _move_proxy_siblings returned (0, ['A001.mov (something is already at the destination)']) for both the plain rename and the case-only rename.

findings.title: Create/link over an ARCHIVED project answers ok but it stays archived and invisible
findings.what: Neither path checks archived_at. The folder and marker survive archiving, so create takes the marker-convergence branch and adopt takes the marker. Both call upsert_project, which keeps an archived row at active=0. The route still returns ok, writes a project.create audit row and can sticky-map a Resolve project onto the hidden slug.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin archives 2026/Shoot. An editor presses NEW PROJECT 2026/Shoot and is told it was created. The project never appears, PUT /selection 404s 'unknown or inactive project', and their Resolve project is mapped to it. Probe: after archive, create and adopt both returned {'slug':'2026-shoot'} with the row still active=0.

findings.title: Local-mode admin password reset does not revoke the account's existing sessions
findings.what: The local branch only UPDATEs password_hash via local_users.set_password. Sessions are server-side rows that never consult the password, so they survive the reset. Disable and delete purge credentials through _purge_user_credentials; reset does not.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin resets a local editor's leaked password. Whoever holds a session opened with the leaked password stays signed in for up to 7 days, able to tick, untick and create projects, unless the admin also finds sessions/revoke.

findings.title: A NAS that does not answer turns a MISSING protection line into a 'this has cleared' mail and closes its notice
findings.what: protection.run_cycle keeps protection_missing notices only for lines BROKEN this pass. A line that drops to NOT_CHECKED because the NAS could not be asked loses its notice, and _check_protection_missing stops returning it while the alerts check itself succeeded, so deliver() records and mails a RECOVERED. invariants.run_cycle has the guard for this (dash-collector-2); protection does not.
findings.failure_scenario: snapshot_tree is MISSING and alerted. The NAS API is down for one invariants pass: the owner is mailed 'This has cleared' about the snapshot schedule, the red card leaves the home page, and a fresh error goes out when the NAS answers again. Every NAS blip flaps the most important safety line. Probe p2.py: recovered=1, a protection_missing.ok row is written and the notice's cleared_at is set.
findings.ledger: new (same shape as the fixed dash-collector-2 for invariants)

findings.title: check_failed alerts can never recover, so they stay open forever and a later failure is reported as weeks old
findings.what: deliver() only offers recovery for kinds in ALERT_KINDS (checked_kinds), and CHECK_FAILED is deliberately outside that registry. No check_failed.ok is ever written, so _is_open('check_failed', kind) is True for ever.
findings.failure_scenario: A check raises once and is mailed. It runs fine afterwards, but no recovery is sent and the ledger still says it is failing. Weeks later it raises again and deliver treats it as a repeat ('still not fixed after 49 day(s)' in digest mode). Probe p1.py: recovered=0, _is_open stays True, _open_days=49. A registry kind in the same sequence recovers.

findings.title: A snapshot restore's .restored-<ts> folder is replicated by Syncthing to every editor who has the project ticked
findings.what: The quarantine directory is created inside the live project folder, a sendreceive Syncthing root with fsWatcher. The project .stignore has no rule for dot-directories or .restored-*, so every non-video file a restore writes is pushed to every full-tick editor. The leading dot only hides it from provision's marker scan.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner restores a project with include-changed. GBs of WAV and .drp files land in .restored-<ts>/ and are pulled to every editor with that project ticked. When the owner deletes the quarantine on the server, the editors' copies stay because of the ignoreDelete retrofit (2026-08-11): a permanent duplicate tree on every laptop, against the page's 'costs disk space and nothing else'.

findings.title: A failed db.migrate in the collector loop is never retried and leaves the collector on the un-migrated connection
findings.what: conn is assigned before db.migrate(conn). When migrate raises, the loop continues with conn no longer None, so the migration the comment says is retried never runs again from this thread, and the connection is kept rather than closed.
findings.failure_scenario: A boot where the collector starts while the app is still migrating: migrate raises 'database is locked', and the collector runs every cycle on a schema it never confirmed. The only symptom is per-cycle failures if the app's own migration also failed.

findings.title: The anonymous first-run window opens every setup route, not only the EULA and create-admin steps
findings.what: Under DASH_AUTH_METHOD=local with no account yet, require_setup_access lets anonymous callers use every /api/v1/setup/* route. That includes saving the alert destination (email or webhook), sending test alerts to any URL, getting a Tailscale sign-in URL through tailnet/run, and running the secrets task. The module's own contract limits the window to the EULA and create-admin steps.
findings.failure_scenario: Before the owner creates the first account on a fresh appliance, another host on the LAN POSTs /api/v1/setup/alerts {webhook: attacker URL}. It is stored, and the collector starts sending fleet alerts there. The same host can POST /setup/tasks/tailnet/run, read the AuthURL, and join the appliance's Tailscale node to its own tailnet.

verification.reason:
The code does what the finding says, but the attack in the failure scenario can't happen on the deployment this applies to.

What holds up: in setup_routes.py, require_setup_access (lines 87-99) and first_run_open (lines 47-84) return None, meaning an anonymous caller is allowed, for every route that calls them. Under DASH_AUTH_METHOD=local with an empty users table, that includes tasks/{id}/run (tailnet, secrets and the rest), tasks/{id}/skip, /setup/alerts and /setup/alerts/test. Two documents say the anonymous window covers only steps 1 and 2: docs/APPLIANCE_INSTALL.md:109 ("Steps 1 and 2 are reachable with no session") and the setup_routes module docstring. So there is a real gap between the code and its written contract. I found no open KNOWN_BUGS entry for it. The tests only check that tasks and eula open and that the window shuts once an admin exists.

Why the severity drops: the scenario needs "another host on the LAN" to reach the dashboard before the first account exists. The only shipped deployment that is local-auth and zero-touch is dashboard/deploy/compose.appliance.yaml. It publishes the dashboard on "127.0.0.1:8480:8480" only. Its own comment says this loopback bind exists so the NAS's own admin can reach the wizard "before the tailnet node has even been signed in -- there is no other way in until it has been". Before tailnet sign-in, nothing on the LAN can reach /api/v1/setup/*. So the LAN attacker can't:
- POST /setup/alerts;
- or call tailnet/run to get the AuthURL and join the node to their own tailnet.

The window stays open after tailnet sign-in until the owner creates the first account. In that period, only members of the owner's own tailnet can reach the page through Serve, and they are already semi-trusted. Anyone on the NAS host itself already has more than this gives. The smb deployments (the TrueNAS compose, default auth_method=smb) and oidc deployments keep the window closed. The window also closes for good when the first account exists (setup_admin re-checks under BEGIN IMMEDIATE).

What remains is a defense-in-depth defect: the code doesn't match the documented steps-1-and-2-only contract, and it only matters if a local-auth dashboard is ever exposed on a non-loopback port before the first account is created. Worth tightening by gating the non-EULA/admin routes on an admin session, but it is not high.

findings.title: The session touch blocks the event loop for up to 20 s and then 500s a valid session
findings.what: The async login_gate and csrf_gate call SessionStore.validate inline. About once a minute per session, validate runs an UPDATE that waits up to 20 s for the database lock while holding a process-wide lock. On the single worker this runs on the event loop. If the database lock is still busy after 20 s, OperationalError propagates as a 500.
findings.failure_scenario: The collector or a large companion report holds the SQLite write lock. The next request from a signed-in browser that is due a touch stops the whole event loop for 20 s: every report and htmx poll stalls. Then that user gets a 500 even though the session is valid. Probe: blocked 21.9 s, then raised 'database is locked'.
findings.ledger: related to CR-282F (fixed for the error handler only)

findings.title: UNDO of a site change empties the project template and the shared asset folder list
findings.what: For template_folders and shared_asset_folders, _settings_fallback returns "", so the diff records an absent row as from="". Undo writes that "" back as an explicit row, and _shape then resolves an empty list instead of the provision defaults.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin imports a site.toml with template_folders/shared_assets, then presses UNDO LAST IMPORT. From then on new projects are created with no template subfolders, and GET /api/v1/site publishes shared_asset_folders: [] to every installer and companion. Probe: 8 template folders and 2 asset folders both became [].

findings.title: A shared asset folder name with no ASCII letter or digit 500s /api/v1/site and every manifest reader
findings.what: _validate_csv never checks that a shared_asset_folders entry can become a folder id. An all-CJK name is saved, and every later resolved_manifest raises ValueError from slugify. Two names that slugify to the same id are also accepted and produce duplicate Syncthing folder ids.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin adds the shared library '音效'. The save commits and its own response 500s. From then on GET /api/v1/site, admin site GET/export, project creation (template_folders) and the setup studio check all 500 until someone fixes the row through the API. Probe confirmed: ValueError: slugify('音效') produced an empty slug.

findings.title: Setup reports the admin step done on an OIDC admin claim that grants nothing
findings.what: With oidc, no DASH_ADMIN_USERS and DASH_OIDC_ADMIN_CLAIM set, _check_admin returns ok. auth.is_admin never reads claims; the claim is logged only, and the docs say it is not obeyed.
findings.failure_scenario: The wizard shows the admin step green on a dashboard where nobody is admin. Break-glass /login?local=1 is also limited to the empty DASH_ADMIN_USERS list, so the only way back in is a redeploy.

findings.title: The boot log misdescribes DASH_COOKIE_SECURE=true/yes/on/false/no/off
findings.what: describe_auth maps only the literal '1' and '0', while cookie_secure also accepts true/yes/on and false/no/off. For those values the boot line says 'Secure follows the request scheme' even though the flag is forced.
findings.failure_scenario: With DASH_COOKIE_SECURE=true behind plain http, the operator reads 'follows the request scheme' in the boot line and rules out the Secure flag, which is the actual cause of the login loop.

findings.title: A trusted proxy's X-Forwarded-For is read from the client-controlled left end
findings.what: client_ip takes the first comma element of X-Forwarded-For from a trusted proxy. A proxy that appends to the header (nginx proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, Go Director-mode proxies) leaves the client-supplied value at the left.
findings.failure_scenario: Behind a trusted nginx, a password sprayer rotates a fake X-Forwarded-For on each attempt and the 40-per-hour IP budget never trips. The same trick can fill an innocent address's budget.

findings.title: A double slash walks past CardsGate: /cards/p/<slug>//api/root reaches engine.set_root()
findings.what: The gate matches the child path literally against /api/root and /api/restart. The BaseHTTPRequestHandler behind it collapses a leading '//' to '/' in parse_request (CPython gh-87389) before dispatching, so '//api/root' is not blocked by the gate but is served by the handler. This is the leading-slash sibling of dash-release-jobs-4, which closed the trailing-slash variant.
findings.failure_scenario: A signed-in session POSTs {root: B} to /cards/p/<slug-A>//api/root. Engine A moves onto episode B, which may already have its own engine: the pool key lies and two engines write one episode from two state directories. //api/restart also reaches restart_server, which on a Windows dev run spawns a copy of the dashboard and calls os._exit(0).

findings.title: An agent's traffic follows whichever of its editor's devices made the last request, so pending and result land on different engines
findings.what: _where holds one slug per editor and is overwritten by every request the dispatcher serves, including polls and media ranges. One account with a laptop in episode A and a phone in episode B (the design's everyday pair) makes it flip several times a second. /state, /pending and /result are each routed on their own lookup, so a long poll and its result can reach different engines.
findings.failure_scenario: The agent's /pending takes edit #12 from engine A and Resolve applies it. /result is routed to engine B, which answers 'that request is no longer open'. A's next poll then reports 'the Resolve agent went away with that edit - it was never confirmed', and the editor re-applies an edit Resolve already made. The probe showed engine_for alternating A,B,A,B.

findings.title: Pinned jobs wait for ever, with no alert, whenever no episode happens to be open
findings.what: The drain thread can only work while pool.any_engine() returns an engine, which is only while somebody has an episode open. A job pinned while an episode was open, followed by that episode closing or the container restarting (the pool starts empty), sits pinned with no worker. None of DDIAG-6's three shapes (not mounted, thread not running, stale in-hand row) matches this one.
findings.failure_scenario: A proxy-480p job is pinned while an editor has an episode open. The editor closes it, or the container restarts overnight. The job never runs, PROBLEMS THE SERVER FOUND stays empty, and why answers reason_code pinned with transient true, so Timeline Cards' client waits instead of making the file itself.
findings.ledger: related to CR-282G (fixed; this is the shape it left)

findings.title: After a session-secret rotation the b-roll and music gates mint no identity, so ingest panels and client folders 401
findings.what: login_gate accepts sessions signed with DASH_SESSION_SECRET_PREVIOUS (DASH-2), but BrollGate and MusicGate re-decode the cookie with the current secret only. Every pre-rotation session therefore reaches the sub-app without X-CCSync-User or X-CCSync-Admin.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin rotates the secret. Signed-in editors still see the dashboard and both searches working, but /broll/api/ingest-batches, /broll/api/client-folders and the music ingest panel answer 401 while the page shows them signed in. Nothing tells them to sign in again. The probe showed read_session_cookie(new) returning None while login_gate's _read_token_any returned the user.

findings.title: The API-path session trim drops corpus parts 2..n once a conversation passes 40 turns
findings.what: _trimmed keeps only messages[:2] plus the last 78. Since a large corpus is sent as one turn per part (montage_open), parts 2..n are the first messages the trim drops. The shifting window also stops the prefix cache from hitting on every later turn.
findings.failure_scenario: A four-part corpus on an API-key site: after about 36 searches, turn 41 is sent without part 2, turn 42 without parts 2-3, and so on. Searches silently stop finding those interviews, and each warm turn re-reads the history at full price.

findings.title: POST /cards/open walks the vault four levels deep on the event loop
findings.what: cards_open is async def, and when the 30 s scan cache has lapsed it calls cards_pool.episodes(), a recursive os.scandir of the vault, directly on the event loop. This breaks the module's own rule that building is not a request. cards_close likewise calls engine.stop() on the loop.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor presses OPEN more than 30 s after drawing the landing page. The single-worker dashboard (fleet reports and every page) blocks on the vault scan, for seconds on a large share and indefinitely if the export hangs.
