findings.title: The 'same Message-ID is in my Sent folder' proof is an IMAP substring search, so a forged From passes the authentication check
findings.what: _in_sent runs SEARCH HEADER Message-ID "<mid>", and RFC 3501 HEADER search is a substring match. It never compares the Sent copy with the reply. handle_message treats a hit as proof of authorship when sender == alerts_smtp_user, and that override applies even when the topmost Authentication-Results says dmarc=fail.
findings.failure_scenario: A forged mail From the owner's smtp-user address To the reply address, with Message-ID 'mail.gmail.com' (a fragment of any message the owner sent) and a CCT token from a report in the last 48 h, reaches INBOX where the domain's DMARC policy is none. The Sent search matches, ok becomes True, and the actions run (release the fleet halt, push updates, cancel jobs).

findings.title: /ytdl drops the identity of every session signed with a previous DASH_SESSION_SECRET
findings.what: login_gate accepts cookies signed with a secret in session_secrets_previous (DASH-2). YtdlGate calls auth.read_session_cookie(self._secret, cookie) with no previous secrets, so no X-CCSync-User is stamped and ytdlweb answers 401.
findings.failure_scenario: After a secret rotation that keeps the old key in the previous list, every editor still gets into the dashboard, but /ytdl returns 401 for everyone until each person logs in again (up to 7 days). Probe: a cookie signed with the old key resolves to 'bob' in login_gate's reader, but YtdlGate stamps no identity header.

findings.title: The ytdl gate reads the FIRST ccsync_session cookie while login_gate reads the LAST, and the gate never checks revocation
findings.what: _session_cookie returns the first duplicate cookie; Starlette's cookie_parser (used by login_gate) keeps the last. The gate checks only the signature and expiry, never the server-side session row, so the identity given to ytdlweb can be a different user, taken from a revoked cookie.
findings.failure_scenario: The browser holds two ccsync_session cookies (a narrower Path is sent first). login_gate authenticates user B's live session, but ytdlweb acts as user A, whose session was revoked. Probe: for 'ccsync_session=FIRST; ccsync_session=LAST', cookie_parser gives LAST and ytdl gives FIRST.

findings.title: crash_report.redact misses the secrets its own docstring names (env-style and quoted keys)
findings.what: The key pattern needs a \b before the key name, which never matches after '_' (TRUENAS_PW, DASH_SESSION_SECRET, SYNCTHING_API_KEY). It also needs [:=] straight after the name, which fails on a quoted dict or JSON key. The same redactor feeds notices.error_detail, so its output reaches the home page and DB backups.
findings.failure_scenario: An exception quoting 'DASH_SESSION_SECRET=...', 'TRUENAS_PW=...' or "{'password': ...}" is written unredacted into a crash file or a notice body. The probe confirmed all five forms come back unchanged.

findings.title: Reply poll cap counts already-handled messages, so an older unhandled reply can be starved forever
findings.what: Since UNSEEN was dropped, the search returns every message in the 2-day window. numbers[-20:] is taken before the already-known skip, so handled messages use up all 20 slots every poll.
findings.failure_scenario: With 20 or more messages to the plus-address in 2 days (replies, or anyone mailing it on purpose), the owner's reply ranked 21st from the newest is never read and ages out of the SINCE window unhandled, with no notice.

findings.title: The CCT reply token is stored in plaintext beside its hash
findings.what: token_hash stores only sha256(token), but _finish persists the mailed body, including 'Reference: CCT-<token>', in triage_runs.report_json. /admin/alerts/triage/{id} serves it, and every DB backup carries it.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone with a copy of dashboard.db (a backup or snapshot) reads a live 48 h token, which is the third reply-authentication factor.

findings.title: Authentication-Results is trusted without checking its authserv-id
findings.what: The code's own comment records that Google adds no Authentication-Results for mail that never leaves the Workspace. In that case the topmost header is whatever the sender wrote, and no authserv-id (e.g. mx.google.com) is checked.
findings.failure_scenario: A message submitted inside the same domain, carrying a hand-written 'Authentication-Results: x; dkim=pass header.d=<domain>' and a From in alerts_smtp_to, passes check 2 with no DKIM ever evaluated.

findings.title: A second CLI update inside the grace hour deletes the still-in-grace version at once
findings.what: _finish_install records only the version it is replacing as previous_version and drops any earlier one still waiting out its grace. _prune_old_versions then rmtrees it straight away.
findings.failure_scenario: UPDATE A to B, then B to C within the hour (admin plus auto-updater). A Cards call started on A just before the first flip loses its binary path mid-run, which is the CR-309 failure the grace period exists to prevent.

findings.title: Two crashes of the same thread in the same second overwrite one crash file
findings.what: The file name is <when to the second>-<thread>.json, opened with O_TRUNC.
findings.failure_scenario: In a burst of exceptions from same-named threads within one second, only the last traceback survives, and the first one is usually the cause.

findings.title: Client-folder item matching ORs a stale stored id with the current name: remove/note hit the wrong clip, add refuses a new one
findings.what: Every matcher is `video_id = ? OR (share, rel_path) = identity_of(?)`, using one number as both a stored-ledger id and a current-index id. After a publish renumbers videos.id, _identity_of(stored_id) resolves to whichever clip now holds that number, and video_id = current_id matches whichever item was stored under it. The panel sends the stored id (not the current one MEDIA-23 assumes).
findings.failure_scenario: Folder holds X (stored 5) and Z (stored 9); a publish renumbers Z->5, X->12. Removing X from the panel (sends 5) deletes both X and Z from the client's live link (probe: before [5 X, 9 Z] -> after []). Same shape writes a note onto two clips and shows the wrong caption on the public detail panel. Inverse: the new clip Y at id 5 cannot be added (probe: add_items([5]) -> added [], already [5]) and the popover ticks it as present.
findings.ledger: new (the MEDIA-23 fix's premise is wrong; related to broll-4 2026-08-21)

findings.title: HttpBackend posts the LOCAL shadow id to /api/ingest/index and /api/ingest/moved, so descriptions land on a different clip and it gets renamed
findings.what: The docstring says local and remote ids are independent id spaces and upsert_video discards the remote id. But write_index_result and record_moved send the local shadow id (which pipeline reads from videos_by_status), and the server looks that number up in the canonical broll.db.
findings.failure_scenario: db.mode: api against an archive of 15,000 clips: the first new local clip is id 1. /ingest/index replaces canonical clip 1's segments/themes/flags/category_hint with the new clip's description and marks it indexed, while the new clip stays discovered with no segments. The sorter's record_moved renames canonical clip 1's rel_path. The search results are silently corrupted. Dormant on the base rig today (sqlite mode).

findings.title: Posters/sprites are keyed by videos.id in one shared folder while the base rig and the live dashboard mint ids independently, and the drain re-mints ingested ids without moving their stills
findings.what: Fleet ingest claims mint ids above the live max, the base rig mints its new clips at the same numbers, and both write <archive>/posters|sprites/<id>.jpg. build_archive replaces a differing file at that name. At publish the drain re-inserts dashboard-ingested clips with new ids, and no step renames their stills.
findings.failure_scenario: 20 dashboard-ingested clips (15001-15020), then the base rig indexes 30 clips (its 15001-15030) and runs build_archive. The fleet clips now show another clip's poster and a mismatched scrub sprite in search and on client share links. After publish + drain they become 15031-15050 and show no preview permanently (originals stashed in the archive trash).

findings.title: A cancelled release is accepted from any of the editor's machines with no leaseholder check, deleting the live holder's in-flight rows
findings.what: For state=cancelled the route checks only batch.editor == editor, never X-CCSync-Machine vs batch.machine or the lease, then release() cancels non-kept items and deletes every `ingesting` video row.
findings.failure_scenario: Machine A slept holding a batch. Its lease expired and machine B (same editor) took the batch over. The editor then cancels in A's stale companion. The server cancels B's running batch and deletes the rows B is uploading into. B's next POST gets a 410, and its uploaded files stay in the archive with no row.

findings.title: The 'share vanished' guard runs after the download phase has created the project folder, so it can never fire
findings.what: _phase_download calls ensure_outdir (os.makedirs of <PROJECTS_ROOT>/<label>/Youtube/<term>) before tree_missing_note. tree_is_gone answers 'not gone' as soon as <PROJECTS_ROOT>/<label> is a directory, which ensure_outdir has just created. So on an empty mount point the CR-286M guard always answers False. _no_room_note's tree check is reached after the same makedirs.
findings.failure_scenario: The NAS dataset is unmounted while the host has room. An editor presses DOWNLOAD and the worker creates the tree in the container overlay, finds it 'present', and downloads every clip there. ledger_add records NAS-relative paths with no file behind them, so every later search or paste of those ids across the fleet is skipped as already held, and the files are lost on the next container recreate. The overlay folder also fools the press-time check on every later press. Probe: tree_is_gone True -> ensure_outdir -> tree_is_gone False, tree_missing_note None.

verification.reason: The mechanism holds exactly as described. In ytdl/web/ytdlweb/worker.py, _phase_download calls ensure_outdir(outdir) at line 1619. That is os.makedirs of PROJECTS_ROOT/<label>/Youtube/<term>, so it creates PROJECTS_ROOT/<label>. The ytdl-web-5 guard runs later (tree_missing_note, line 1683), and so does _no_room_note's own tree_missing_note call (line 1567). Both reach routes_api.tree_is_gone (routes_api.py:1638), whose first test is `if project_dir.is_dir(): return False`. The directory ensure_outdir just made passes that test. So once the job reaches the guard, the guard always answers "not gone": on an emptied mount point the worker downloads into the container overlay and ledger_add records NAS-relative paths, which is the very scenario the ytdl-web-5 comment says it prevents. The folder left in the overlay then also makes the press-time _refuse_if_the_tree_is_gone answer "present" on every later press. Nothing earlier guards this: tree_is_gone/tree_missing_note are called only from these two worker sites and from the disk_full-only press path. KNOWN_BUGS has no open entry and nothing intends this behaviour. The regression test (tests/test_bug_hunt_2026_09_18_webapps_tools.py:128-137) calls only the helper, never _phase_download, which is why the ordering bug passes the gate. The fix is to move the tree check before ensure_outdir (and _sweep_stale). High stands: silent loss of downloads plus a poisoned fleet dedupe ledger, and a recorded fix that is dead code. It needs an unmounted dataset to trigger, but that failure is exactly what this guard exists for.

findings.title: A browser upload can take a filename a fleet batch already promised, and the companion's upload then overwrites it
findings.what: A fleet result reserves dest_name (ingest_items plus a tracks row) until the companion's queued upload lands, which can be minutes later or hours later if uploads are paused. allocate_name checks new names against the disk, the reservation ledger and tracks. The browser queued-ingest path uses db.unique_dest, which checks only the disk. The companion uploads with plain rclone copyto, with no --ignore-existing.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor A's companion posts the result for theme.wav (row written, upload queued). Editor B drops a different theme.wav in the browser and unique_dest gives it the same name, so it is moved into the library and queued. A's rclone copyto then overwrites it, and mark_uploaded sees A's size and marks it live. B's recording is gone from the library with no error, and B's queue row points at A's audio.

verification.reason: The mechanism holds. When a fleet result is posted, allocate_name (ingest_batches.py:226-280) reserves dest_name in three places: the ledger, the tracks table and the disk (_candidate_free, which checks the reserved set, then _disk_state, then _track_state). The companion's upload lands in the same flat share root, which is music_ingest's LIBRARY_REMOTE_REL (the plan doc says "uploads stay flat under share_root()"). The browser queued-ingest path (routes_ingest.py:377, via _ingest_one) calls db.unique_dest (db.py:524-535), and that loop only checks safe_join(root, cand).exists(). It does not look at the ledger or the tracks table. So while a fleet track's upload is still pending (the tracks row exists, the file is not on disk yet), a browser drop with the same name is handed the same name and moved into the library. The companion then uploads with plain `rclone copyto` (broll_upload.py:180-190), with no --ignore-existing flag. rclone writes a .partial and renames it over B's file. mark_uploaded stats the file, sees A's size and marks it live. B's queue row (rel_path theme.wav) now points at A's audio, and when it is indexed it will collide with A's tracks row, which shares that rel_path. KNOWN_BUGS.md and the docs have no entry for this, and the allocate_name docstring itself says unique_dest looks at disk only. Downgraded from high because two separate ingests (a fleet batch and a browser drop) have to use the same final filename inside the upload window. And what is lost is the library copy: B's original is still on B's machine, so it can be re-ingested once someone notices. It is still silent and wrong, so it is a real defect at medium.

findings.title: The first fleet drop into a new library refuses itself from item 2 onward
findings.what: share_root_ready samples the 25 newest and 25 oldest tracks rows and calls the share not mounted when none of them is on disk. A fleet result writes its row before the audio is uploaded, and uploads run separately from embedding. In a library whose only rows come from the drop in progress, both ends of the sample are unlanded rows.
findings.failure_scenario: A new customer's first companion drop: item 1's result passes (empty table), then item 2 gets 503 share_not_ready 'there but empty ... not mounted' until item 1's upload lands. With uploads paused, or a slow first upload, each item uses up its retry budget and fails permanently, with a message blaming a healthy mount. Probe: empty table (True,''), one unlanded row (False, 'is there but empty ...').
findings.ledger: related to CR-262E (fixed; the fix does not cover a library made only of in-flight rows)

findings.title: Cancelling a batch strands every indexed-but-not-uploaded track as a permanent row with no audio
findings.what: release(state='cancelled') sets indexed and uploading items, which already have a tracks row, to cancelled. The docstring promises they stay 'indexed ... fixable by re-uploading'. cancelled is terminal, retry_failed only moves failed items, and nothing on the NAS deletes the row (only a manual base-rig --prune).
findings.failure_scenario: An editor cancels a drop halfway through, or the sweep finalises a cancelled batch whose machine died. The embedded-but-not-uploaded tracks stay in tracks for good: they appear in search, similar and browse, /api/audio answers 404 'file missing', they skew the percentiles, tags and debias axes, and they hold their filenames. findings.title: publish_db.py --rollback picks the .prev-<ts>-wal sidecar and renames it over the live index
findings.what: The publish moves the live file's -wal/-shm along with it, to <target>.prev-<ts>-wal/-shm. The listing is find -name '<file>.prev-*', which matches those sidecars too. newest_prev sorts by name and takes the last one, and '...T101500' < '...-shm' < '...-wal', so the newest prev is the -wal file whenever the swapped-out index had a WAL beside it (the normal case, because the container holds it open in WAL mode).
findings.failure_scenario: After a bad publish the operator runs the documented recovery, publish_db.py --which broll --rollback --apply. The script moves the live broll.db aside and runs mv broll.db.prev-<ts>-wal broll.db, which installs a WAL journal as the database. It prints 'rolled back', and /broll (or /music) is serving a file that is not a database. Probe: newest_prev on a realistic listing returned '/d/broll.db.prev-20260821T101500-wal'. The only test lists bare .prev names, so it would not catch this.

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. The publish swap (install_dashboard_app.build_db_swap_script, around lines 3322-3339) moves <target>-wal and <target>-shm to <old>-wal and <old>-shm, where old = <target>.prev-<stamp> (publish_db.py:916). list_prev_command (publish_db.py:554-556) runs find -name '<file>.prev-*', which also matches those sidecars. newest_prev (:576-577) sorts the lines as plain strings and takes the last one. A bare name is a prefix of its own sidecar names, so '...T101500' sorts before '...T101500-shm', which sorts before '...T101500-wal'. I ran that sort on a realistic listing in the dashboard venv, and it returned /d/broll.db.prev-20260821T101500-wal.

The WAL sidecar is there in the normal case. The container holds the index open read-write in WAL mode (CLAUDE.md), and the swap is a rename done under the running container, so the -wal file exists when the swap happens.

build_rollback_script (:513-538) then does the following:
- The existence check on prev passes.
- It moves live broll.db and its sidecars aside.
- It runs mv <prev>-wal broll.db.
- It looks for <prev>-wal-wal and <prev>-wal-shm to bring back. They do not exist, so it skips them.
- It prints 'rolled back'.

The live path now holds a WAL journal instead of a database, and the real .prev file stays where it was.

Nothing guards against this:
- No check in do_rollback rejects a -wal/-shm suffix.
- The only test (tests/test_bug_hunt_2026_08_21.py:68) lists bare .prev names.
- No KNOWN_BUGS entry covers it.

The workaround is --from-prev with an explicit path. But the default path is the documented first-line recovery (BACKUP_RESTORE 4d), which runs right after a bad publish, and it replaces the live b-roll/music index with a file that is not a database while reporting success. High stands.

findings.title: ship.cmd -Resume cannot resume past the publish and tells the operator to bump the version

Following that advice fails at step 0 with 'companion vX is ALREADY published ... bump VERSION'. The same happens after a failed local upgrade. --version --reason ... --github-upload. But --retract takes a single KIND/PLATFORM/VERSION value, and the line also leaves out the required --feed-dir and --github-repo.

findings.title: The "Resolve relinked after all" answer is dropped by the dashboard, so a move shows "Resolve not repointed yet" for ever

findings.title: A session-secret rotation drain keeps the report and jobs alive but cuts every un-re-signed machine out of b-roll ingest, music ingest and ytdl
findings.what: The dashboard's report, jobs and cards-tunnel routes accept identity tokens signed with DASH_SESSION_SECRET_PREVIOUS through read_identity_token_ex. The three mounted apps verify X-CCSync-Identity against DASH_SESSION_SECRET only, and the gates pass that header through unchanged.

findings.title: Lane last_error/detail/current_project caps still raise, and the companion never caps them: one long lane error 422s the whole report

findings.title: /verify builds its upgrade offer without the arch, the machine or the withheld reason, and sign_in adopts it as if it were a report reply

findings.title: A computer whose hostname is not Latin-1 cannot make any b-roll or music ingest fleet call

findings.title: The wizard still takes a machine's role from the PERSON, so a re-run dismantles an admin's remote laptop and loops a non-admin's wired desktop
findings.where: onboarding/steps.py:1752 (effective_install_role), onboarding/steps.py:3160 (ensure_config forces mode), onboarding/onboard.py:785-795,866-871; installer/windows_bootstrap.ps1:1428
findings.what: /verify answers role=base for every admin and editor for everyone else. The wizard lets that override the radio pick, forces it into config.toml `mode`, and chooses the cleanup plan and the worker from it. Since CR-88 (0.9.54) wired/remote is the computer's own setting and the person's role is diagnostics only, so the wizard is now the last place that turns the person's role into the machine's mode. The amber note's claim that the companion 'obeys anyway' is false.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Admin re-runs onboard.exe on his remote laptop and picks REMOTE EDITOR. The wizard runs a base install: config becomes mode=base and local_root=P:\, and the base cleanup deletes the CCSyncSyncthing and CCSyncSubstP Run values and the CCSync-SubstP task. After a reboot there is no P:, Syncthing does not start and nothing syncs, while the finish page says DONE: CONNECTED TO THE NAS. (b) A non-admin on a wired desktop picks PHYSICALLY CONNECTED and gets an editor install. The foreign-P: refusal tells them to re-run and pick PHYSICALLY CONNECTED, and the wizard overrides that choice again, so every run ends the same way.
findings.ledger: related to CR-66 (deferred data-model-2); CR-88 has since removed the justification for deferring it

verification.reason:
The mechanism is real. dashboard api.py:2226 still sends `"role": "base" if auth.is_admin(...) else "editor"`. onboarding/steps.py:1752 `effective_install_role` lets any recognised verified role beat the radio button. onboard.py:802-806 snaps role_var to that role, and steps.py:3165 `ensure_config` forces it into config.toml `mode` (for base it also sets local_root and canonical_prefix to the base root). Since CR-88, companion app.py:4795 `effective_mode` reads config `mode` only, so the wizard is now the one place where the person's role becomes the machine's mode. That also makes the amber note at onboard.py:858-861 ("which the companion obeys anyway") stale and wrong. Scenarios (a) and (b) follow from the code.

It is not a new high, though. This is the known, ledgered, deliberately deferred item: bug-hunt-2026-08-21 data-model-2 names this exact function and both consequences (admin remote laptop syncs nothing; non-admin wired editor forced into an editor install) with "Status: deferred by decision (CR-66)". KNOWN_BUGS CR-66 lists it among "deliberately deferred, with reasons". docs/MULTI_BASE_RIG_PLAN.md:67-68 and section WP5 say "The precedence half of WP5 is not built" and spell out the planned inversion (radio wins). CR-88 fixed the companion half only.

Other reasons to lower it:
- The trigger is narrow: an admin re-running onboard.exe on a second, remote machine, or a non-admin on a wired desktop.
- The companion's Settings -> THIS COMPUTER can now flip `mode` back without hand-editing TOML.
- In case (b) the foreign-P: refusal stops the destructive teardown instead of letting it run.

What is new since the deferral is the false amber copy and the fact that the companion no longer self-corrects. Those are worth recording against the existing entry rather than as a fresh high.

findings.title: On a site with the shared report token retired, the wizard says DONE for a machine with no fleet credential

findings.title: windows_upgrade.ps1 sends a licence-only problem to the full reinstall wizard, alongside the companion's own licence dialog

findings.title: A laptop that is merely asleep gets a red "Upload has stopped" headline after 15 minutes

findings.title: The per-kind manifest cap still makes phantom proxy downloads, the UI says 'may undercount', and safe-to-close can miss uploads
findings.what: With more than 2000 proxies or originals per project on one machine, only the first 2000 in walk order are reported. The down diff counts every proxy past the cap as owed (an OVERcount that never clears), yet the row says 'totals may undercount'. The up diff undercounts originals past the cap, so safe_to_close can say 'Safe to close' while unuploaded originals exist.
findings.failure_scenario: A project grows to 2,300 proxies, all on the editor's drive: [ QUEUED ] shows 'proxy download, 300 files' for ever (the CR-314 phantom at a higher number). A 2,400-clip project whose new card falls past the cap: the page says 'Safe to close: nothing of yours is waiting'.

findings.title: Tray says 'downloading N files' and pulses amber for ever when lane C has no connected peer
findings.what: Lane C reports STATE_SYNCING with queued=needTotalItems regardless of whether any peer is connected, and never sets a progress_token, so the dashboard's SYS-1 stall rule cannot fire. app._lane_peer_states already knows lane C has no peer, and only the power guards use it. findings.failure_scenario: The NAS Syncthing is down or the tailnet path drops with 40 items owed. The fleet lane chip stays amber with no stall verdict.

findings.title: Disk-floor park never clears on its own: the trash prune stops at 1x the floor, the latch clears at 2x
findings.what: The disk-pressure prune deletes trash only until free >= min_free_bytes (20 GB). DiskFloorLatch clears only at 2x (40 GB). The prune therefore stops exactly where the latch is still parked, and neither mechanism can leave the state. The dashboard disk chip text also still claims the trash cannot prune while proxy download is stopped, which is false since SYNC-16 (only the breaker blocks it).
findings.failure_scenario: An SSD at 12 GB free with 35 GB in .ccsync-trash: lane B parks, the prune deletes to about 20.5 GB and stops, and the latch needs 40 GB. Proxy download stays stopped indefinitely with about 26 GB of the product's own trash on the drive. RESUME runs one pass, which fills the drive back under the floor and parks again.

findings.title: 'Idle, nothing owed' is claimed without consulting what is owed
findings.what: The fleet row's all-clear headline is decided from lane states alone. It never reads the owed backlog that fetch_sync_backlog computes for the transfers page, and lanes are idle between sequencer rotations.
findings.failure_scenario: Between passes, with 60 originals owed in a non-current project, the fleet grid says 'Idle, nothing owed' while the same editor's transfers page says 'Not yet: 60 file(s) still uploading from DESKTOP-X'.

findings.title: Tray counts lane C files twice ('up 40 · down 40'); drive reminder nags about downloads the dashboard calls safe
findings.what: _sync_line adds lane C's one count to both up and down. The CR-92 reminder counts lane B proxy downloads and lane C items (and a 0/0 syncing lane B pass as 1) as unfinished work, contradicting the dashboard's uploads-only safe-to-close rule.
findings.failure_scenario: A 40-file audio pull reads 'up 40 · down 40 files'. An editor who pulls the SSD mid proxy-download gets 'disconnected before syncing finished: 1 proxy download still to go' every 30 minutes until home, while the dashboard says 'Safe to close'.

findings.title: Unticking a bucket-inherited project is a no-op that answers changed=true, and the tray then removes it from the person's other computers
findings.what: remove_selection(machine=M) materialises the bucket and deletes M's row. If that leaves M with no rows of its own, selections_for_machine hands it the bucket again, and the bucket still holds the project, because it is never cleared once a person has machines. The companion's untick sees the slug still listed and widens to the person-wide DELETE. That also deletes the other computer's own row, which is the outcome comp-lane-c-2 was meant to prevent.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin ticks B before any report, so it sits in the bucket. DESK gets its own plan [B,A]; LAP inherits [B]. A grid untick of B on LAP returns changed=true, the box shows empty, LAP keeps syncing B, and B comes back on reload. The tray's 'Remove B from this machine' on LAP widens to a person-wide delete: DESK's own B row goes and B is unshared from the desktop within 60 s with no explanation. The same happens when a machine unticks its last own project.
findings.ledger: new (dash-core-1 fixed only the first-own-row case)

verification.reason:
I reproduced it on a scratch DB using the dashboard venv and the real db functions. Setup: B is ticked into the bucket before any report; DESK and LAP are registered; A is ticked on DESK. That gives DESK=[B,A] and LAP=[B]. Then remove_selection(B, machine=LAP) returns True, and selections_for_machine(LAP) still returns [B]. The reason is in db.py:6841-6852: materialise_bucket copies [B] onto LAP and the DELETE takes out that one row, which leaves LAP with no rows of its own. selections_for_machine (db.py:7336-7339) then falls back to the bucket, and nothing ever clears it once a person has machines. The API returns this view with changed=true (api.py:2669-2677). The companion's untick (selection.py:499) then finds B still in the view and sends the person-wide DELETE. On my scratch DB that removed DESK's own B row (DESK went from [B,A] to [A]), so B is unshared from the desktop.

The mechanism is real, I found no guard against it, and KNOWN_BUGS has no open entry for it. The dash-core-1 fix at line 1689 introduced this edge; it did not cover it. The same happens whenever a machine removes its last own row while the bucket is non-empty.

Why medium and not high: every failure here under-shares (a plan row is removed and a Syncthing folder is unshared). No media is deleted, and re-ticking recovers it. It also needs the bucket-plus-several-machines shape, which is a migration/compat state. Even so, one computer's plan silently changing another computer's is a real logic defect, and the dashboard grid untick is a no-op that still answers changed=true.

findings.title: Project page's person-level mode buttons tick the project onto computers that never had it, with no confirm or capacity check
findings.what: SWITCH TO FULL SYNC and SWITCH TO UPLOAD ONLY post ?mode= with no machine, which runs add_selection_for_person. That INSERTs a tick in the chosen mode on every non-wired computer of the person, and also flattens a 'mixed' plan. The buttons show neither the UX-1 capacity confirm nor the list of machines they will touch.
findings.failure_scenario: A project is ticked upload-only on LAP only. Pressing SWITCH TO FULL SYNC switches LAP to full AND adds a new full tick on DESK, which then downloads every proxy (possibly hundreds of GB) with no warning. Probe output: [('LAP','pa','full'),('DESK','pa','full')].

findings.title: Section 4b trashes a whole local folder including never-uploaded originals; trash is kept 14 days, not the documented year
findings.what: When the destination is not synced on this machine, apply_move moves the whole source path into .ccsync-trash. It does not check whether the folder holds originals that lane A has not uploaded yet, and it answers ok=True. The design promises the copy is 'recoverable for a year', but prune_trash defaults to 14 days, and the size cap and disk-pressure rule can prune sooner.
findings.failure_scenario: An upload-only laptop is part-way through uploading X/Card_07. The owner moves Card_07 on the NAS into project Y, which the laptop does not sync. The whole local folder goes to trash, and lane A never uploads from trash. The clips that were never uploaded are then deleted by prune_trash after 14 days, while the project page shows this machine as done.
findings.ledger: new (res-fleet-3 branch; comp-sync-1 fixed only the empty-plan trigger)

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. In companion/src/ccsync_companion/file_moves.py:522-568, apply_move takes the section 4b branch whenever _dest_is_synced_here is False. That branch moves the whole `src` (for an is_dir move, the entire local folder) into .ccsync-trash/<stamp>/Projects/... with src.replace(trash). It records an intent row with new_local="" and returns (True, DETAIL_NOT_SYNCED_HERE, None).

Nothing checks whether the local folder holds files the NAS does not have, meaning originals lane A has not uploaded yet. The caller (app.py around 8160-8196) records ok=True, answers the dashboard with state not_synced_here, and does no pending-upload check.

The dashboard sends the command to the right machines for this to happen. db.file_move_target_machines (db.py:5842) sends it to "every computer syncing the source project in either mode", which includes upload_only, plus machines whose manifest holds the path. So an upload-only machine that is mid-upload of a card folder the owner moves on the NAS into a project it does not sync gets the whole folder trashed. That includes the clips the NAS never received. Lane A only walks Projects/, so it never uploads from .ccsync-trash, and the intent row also excludes the old path from lane A.

Retention does not match the design. docs/HAND_MOVES_ON_THE_SERVER.md:95 promises "recoverable for a year". lane_guard.DEFAULT_TRASH_MAX_AGE_DAYS is 14, and prune_trash also prunes older batches when the trash passes the 50 GB cap or the disk is under pressure. The only exceptions are the newest batch and a tripped breaker.

On the ordinary move branch, un-uploaded files travel to a destination this machine syncs and lane A uploads them from there. Only 4b loses them. I found no KNOWN_BUGS entry covering un-uploaded content in the 4b trash. The res-fleet-3 and comp-sync-1/2 entries cover the empty plan, the proxies and the relink-to-trash, not this.

The trigger is narrow: an admin or hand move of a folder while some machine still has un-uploaded originals in it, and that machine does not sync the destination. The outcome is silent, permanent loss of originals that may be the only copy, while the project page records the machine as having followed the move. So high stands.

findings.title: A file moved out of a borrowed (shared) folder is never announced to the machines that borrow it
findings.what: Move targets are machines ticking the source project plus machines whose editor_media lists the file. A borrower machine is in neither set: its manifest builds per-file lists only for selected projects, never for borrowed lender rels. It still runs lane A over the borrowed subpath, and lane A never deletes. So the comp-sync-3 exclusion fix never gets a command to act on. The same rule also drops unticked machines from the targets 14 days after the untick, when their stale per-file rows are pruned.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor on borrower P drops drone_04.mov into the borrowed Lender/Shared B-roll folder, and lane A uploads it. The owner moves it on the NAS to Lender/Selects. Lender machines follow; P's laptop is never told, and its next borrowed lane A run uploads the file back to Shared B-roll.

findings.title: Companion's unknown-machine untick fallback never fires; unknown hostname gets a silent 200 no-op
findings.what: untick() falls back to the person-wide DELETE only on a 404. api_untick never validates ?machine=: it deletes 0 rows and answers 200 changed=false. The companion ignores 'changed', reports 'unticked', and the tray proceeds to remove the local copy.
findings.failure_scenario: A renamed PC inside SYS-18a's deferred-adoption window uses the tray's 'Remove X from this machine'. The machine-scoped DELETE under the new name removes nothing, and the tray clears the local folder anyway. After adoption, the old plan still holds X, so X downloads again.

findings.title: RETRY FAILED and 'run FIX ALL again' copy the whole file in a second time when only the relink failed
findings.what: Relink-failed and partial-relink results already have a copy in the tree (copied_to set), but they go into _failed_rows. RETRY FAILED re-runs fix_clip from the start, and _claim_destination_path makes `name (2).ext` and copies the full file again. Nothing reuses the copy already made.
findings.failure_scenario: A 40 GB BRAW whose ReplaceClip returns False, or a CANCEL ALL during the relinks: each RETRY FAILED press or later popup adds another full copy (A001 (2).braw, (3) ...). Lane A uploads each one and lane C fans them out to the fleet. Probe: three fix_clip calls gave three copies.

findings.title: UNDO LAST FIX only undoes the last 2-minute burst of a FIX ALL, and a second press falsely says the clips left the media pool
findings.what: Journal sessions end after 120 s with no edit. FIX ALL relinks each clip after its own copy, so any copy over about 4 GB (or any cloud hydration) splits one FIX ALL into many sessions. undo_last_relink replays only the newest session and never marks it undone, so a second press finds nothing at the new paths and reports 'N could not be undone: those clips are no longer in this project's media pool'.
findings.failure_scenario: FIX ALL on 12 large camera clips gives about 12 journal files. UNDO LAST FIX puts back 1 clip. A second press tells the editor the clips have left the media pool (false). The other 11 relinks cannot be reached from the tray, and the button never goes away. Probe: a 10-min gap split 4 relinks into 2 sessions.

findings.title: Share LUTs offers Resolve's factory LUTs, and a Resolve version mismatch turns that into a permanent offer that copies nothing
findings.what: stray_luts scans Resolve's factory LUT folder with no factory exclusion, so SHARE copies all shipped LUTs into the shared library. The module docstring forbids that because they then show twice. A match needs the same name and size, so on a machine with a different Resolve build the factory LUTs count as strays for ever, while copy_into_library skips each one because the dest exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Already live: P:\Assets\Luts holds ACES, Arri, Blackmagic Design, DCI, Canon Log to Rec709.ilut etc., matching this rig's factory folder, so every editor's LUT browser lists them twice. An editor on another Resolve version gets a Share LUTs item that never clears and always answers 'Shared 0 LUTs'.

findings.title: With no matched project, FIX ALL's default destination is the tree root, which lane A never uploads, yet the dialog reports Fixed
findings.what: pick_project_prefix falls back to active_project (blank by default) and then to '', and suggest_destination then gives B-roll/Editor Added/<editor> at the root of local_root, outside Projects/. CORE-H3 already documents that lane A never uploads there. The CORE-H3 fix removed the bare dropdown entries but left the bare default.
findings.failure_scenario: Resolve project 'Rough cut v3' matches no tree dir and the dashboard has no mapping. FIX ALL copies 30 clips to D:\Creators_Club\B-roll\Editor Added\ruskin, relinks, says Fixed and closes. The clips never reach the NAS or other editors, which is the exact problem the dialog promised to solve.

findings.title: A relink stopped part way is reported as 'you skipped it, nothing was copied in or relinked', with no undo pointer
findings.what: A partial_relink result (copy on disk, some clips relinked) has aborted=True, so the popup counts it as a skip and says nothing was copied or relinked and the half-copied files were deleted. The UNDO_POINTER only shows when some result is ok.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor cancels during the relinks. The screen says nothing changed, so they neither check nor undo, while the copy uploads and some clips point at it. summarize_fix_results gives '0 of 1 copied in, 1 skipped by you'.

findings.title: The "fleet-wide stop expired" alert can never fire
findings.what: _check_fleet_halt_expired requires halt['active'] and halt['expired'], but db._halt_state sets active = active and not expired, so the two can never both be true. The check always returns [].
findings.failure_scenario: A halt set Friday expires Saturday and the fleet resumes. The fleet_halt_expired alert that is meant to tell the owner never fires: no mail and nothing in the weekly report, even though the check is registered.

findings.title: The halt's release time reads "releases itself 0s ago", on every page
findings.what: The future expires_at is rendered through the `ago` filter, which clamps negative deltas to 0, so every future expiry prints '0s ago'.
findings.failure_scenario: During a halt, every page shows 'it releases itself 0s ago unless somebody keeps it on'. Nobody can tell when the 24 h stop ends, and it reads as if syncing has already resumed.

findings.title: An expired fleet stop leaves a banner on every page that nothing in the UI can clear
findings.what: An expired halt stays expired=True on every read, and the every-page banner shows it to all users. In the expired state the admin panel offers only [ STOP ALL SYNCING ]. The only thing that clears it is active=0, which the UI posts only from the active state.
findings.failure_scenario: After an expiry, every editor sees 'THE FLEET-WIDE STOP HAS EXPIRED' for weeks. To remove it, the owner must stop the whole fleet again and then release it, which briefly halts every computer.

findings.title: After a restore, the recovery page still shows the same files as missing and invites the same restore again
findings.what: The restore writes to <project>/.restored-<ts>/, and _walk skips dot-dirs, so the next preview reports the same N missing and offers the restore again. The result names only a dot-folder, which is hidden by default over SMB and in Finder, with 'move what you want back yourself' as the only guidance.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner restores 312 files, sees nothing new in Explorer, previews again, is told the same 312 are missing, and restores again. That makes a duplicate copy on the pool, and the files are still not where Resolve looks.

findings.title: When only "changed" files exist, the restore form's defaults are refused, and the confirm quotes the wrong count
findings.what: The form is shown when changed_count > 0 with the include_changed box unticked. The confirm quotes only missing_count ('Copy 0 file(s)'), and the restore then refuses with 'nothing to restore' without naming the checkbox.
findings.failure_scenario: Preview: 0 missing, 1 different. The owner clicks restore, confirms 'Copy 0 file(s)', and is told there is nothing to restore.

findings.title: The Packages page tells a customer's admin to run tools\ship.cmd, a vendor-only script
findings.what: Five owner-facing texts give tools\ship.cmd and docs/RELEASE.md as the next action, whatever the deployment. release_feed.py already makes the same kind of text conditional on image_mode. A customer site has neither and should be pointed to the vendor feed check.
findings.failure_scenario: A fresh customer appliance shows 'nothing is being served yet: publish ... from your wired computer with tools\ship.cmd'. The admin has no such script, and the vendor-feed button that would help is not named.

findings.title: Cancelling a pinned job says "the computer running it" will stop it, but this server runs it
findings.what: request_job_cancel returns 'requested' for claimed, running and pinned jobs alike, and the notice always says a computer will stop it on its next report. Pinned jobs run on the dashboard's own worker.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner cancels a pinned proxy job and is told to wait for a computer's report. No computer holds the job, so he looks for one that does not exist.

findings.title: A mount a site deliberately left OFF raises a permanent 'check the bind mounts' warning
findings.what: Every status other than 'mounted' becomes a feature_not_mounted warn card, including 'disabled': the mounts' own word for 'not asked for' (YouTube off in the vendor build, Cards not configured). The fix text says to check the bind mounts and restart, which cannot clear it.
findings.failure_scenario: A vendor-build customer with YouTube off and no Cards has two warn cards on PROBLEMS THE SERVER FOUND for the life of the install. Restarting the container, as the card says, brings both straight back.

findings.title: versions_behind counts staged/feed builds, so a computer on the CURRENT build is told to UPDATE NOW
findings.what: 'Newer' includes staged (soak-held) packages and every vendor-feed version. A machine already on current is 'N releases behind', and the fix [ UPDATE NOW ] pushes the build it already runs. triage_actions' push_update validator refuses that too.
findings.failure_scenario: Studio state: macOS current 0.9.70 with 0.9.71/72/74 staged. leso/Mac gets 'is 3 releases behind (running 0.9.70, current is 0.9.70)... press UPDATE NOW'. The button does nothing and the alert stays. Probe la2.py reproduces it.

findings.title: platform_channel_stale says 'build it' when the Mac build already exists staged, and names repo commands on customer sites
findings.what: The check never looks for a published-but-staged build on the lagging platform. It always says 'nothing will offer it until somebody builds it' and hard-codes release_macos.sh --publish commands, which are wrong when the build is staged (the publish is refused as a duplicate) and impossible on a feed-fed customer site that has no repo.
findings.failure_scenario: Windows current 0.9.74, macOS current 0.9.70 with 0.9.74 staged (soak gate). The owner is mailed terminal commands to build a Mac release that only needs making current on Packages. Probe la3.py reproduces it.

findings.title: Replies to all-clear/fallback server-check emails are refused and leave a warn card with an impossible fix
findings.what: Every report and the fallback are sent with Reply-To set to the reply address, but only reports that offer actions carry a CCT- reference. An authenticated owner's reply to an all-clear is refused under 'reference', opens a triage_reply_refused warn card saying 'reply to the most recent server check email', and gets no answer. The card stays until an acted reply from the same address, or 7 days.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner replies 'thanks' to the 06:00 all-clear. No confirmation comes back and a warn card appears on the home page for up to a week, then shows up in the next check's evidence. Probe la4.py reproduces it.

findings.title: Invariant 9 is OK when any snapshot task exists, checks the dashboard's dataset, and its fix names the tree
findings.what: The check passes on any enabled task anywhere on the NAS and checks only DASH_UPDATE_SNAPSHOT_DATASET, yet its fix says to snapshot the project tree dataset. It can be green while protection.snapshot_tree says the tree is MISSING.
findings.failure_scenario: The NAS has one hourly task on the dashboard dataset and none on the footage. The Invariants page says 'the customer's data is on a snapshot schedule' while the protection line says the tree is unprotected. A broken verdict about the dashboard dataset sends the owner to snapshot the tree.

findings.title: Invariants collector job is permanently amber ('2 not checked here')
findings.what: Two invariants have a static skip_reason, so every pass counts 2 NOT_CHECKED. _note always returns text and collector_health renders any note as amber, contradicting _note's own 'None on a clean pass' contract.
findings.failure_scenario: The collector health panel shows the invariants job amber on every site forever, which trains the owner to ignore the amber that a real 'invariant broken' note would also show.

findings.title: file_move_detected with zero followers keeps its card for 7 days
findings.what: The CR-320 evidence returns '' when a detected move has no targets, so the card waits out the 7-day quiet period, although a move with no computer holding the file is complete as soon as it is detected.
findings.failure_scenario: Hand moves on the base rig (which works off the NAS) or of server-only files each leave an info card saying 'Nothing to do' on the home page for a week, not 24 h.

findings.title: Disk alerts for a computer that syncs nothing name an impossible consequence and fix
findings.what: disk_low (error, mailed daily) and machine_disk_low ignore the plan and role. For a nothing-ticked or wired computer they say proxy download will leave the editor unable to work and tell the owner to untick a project.
findings.failure_scenario: alex/Razer with nothing ticked and low free space gets a daily error mail about proxy download and an untick fix that has no target.

findings.title: Reply poll caps at the newest 20 BEFORE skipping handled messages; older replies are never read
findings.what: The search now returns handled messages too (no UNSEEN), and the slice is taken before known Message-IDs are skipped. Every poll therefore takes the same newest 20, and the comment 'the rest wait for the next poll' is false.
findings.failure_scenario: A burst of mail to the +address pushes the owner's earlier reply out of the newest 20. It is never acted on, refused or mentioned, and it ages out of the 2-day window.

findings.title: After an index rebuild, removing one client-folder clip can delete a second clip, and adding a clip can be refused as 'already'
findings.what: Item matching is `video_id = X OR (share,rel_path) = identity-of-X-in-the-CURRENT-index`. After publish_db renumbers videos.id, a stored item id can be the current id of a different clip. The panel sends the stored id, _identity_of turns it into another clip's path, and the OR matches a second item. The same collision makes add_items answer 'already' for a new clip, shows a false 'in this folder' tick, and can give the public detail panel another clip's note.
findings.failure_scenario: Folder holds A (stored id 5) and B (stored id 9). Rebuild gives A=7, B=5, new C=9. Adding C returns {'added': [], 'already': [9]}, so C is never added and no error appears. Removing A (DELETE items/5) deletes A and B from the client's live link. The probe printed exactly this: 'panel after: []'.
findings.ledger: new; related to broll-4 (2026-08-21) and MEDIA-23 (2026-08-28), whose OR causes this

findings.title: settle_intents calls a stand-in 'the real original' for any heavy original of 1080 lines or less
findings.what: An intent row is settled by comparing the probed width x height with the ORIGINAL's geometry, on the premise that a stand-in cannot match it. The preview is scaled to min(1080, ih) and never upscaled, so for a 1920x1080 original the preview is also 1920x1080. A 1080p original is heavy, and so gets a stand-in, when its bitrate is over 12 Mbps or its codec is not h264/hevc/prores.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor sends a 1080p 50 Mbps or DNxHD clip and closes the tab mid-sync. The fetch lands unobserved, settle_intents probes 1920x1080 == 1920x1080, logs 'the real original arrived', and deletes the row. The preview's 1080p H.264 bytes are now under the original's name with no ledger entry: the next insert imports them as the original and a render on that machine renders the preview (the proxy-tiers-1 outcome).

findings.title: Cancelling a music batch mid-upload leaves tracks that stay searchable but have no audio and cannot be retried
findings.what: The tracks row (embedding, windows, peaks) is written at result (item 'indexed') before the audio is uploaded. release(state='cancelled') marks indexed and uploading items 'cancelled' (terminal) while their tracks rows stay. That contradicts release's own docstring ('indexed rather than live... fixable by re-uploading'), and retry_failed only moves 'failed' items.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor cancels a 40-track drop during the uploads. Every indexed but not uploaded track stays in music search, facets, tag percentiles and debias axes, its audio 404s and send-to-Resolve fails. The name stays taken (re-drop gives 'theme (2).mp3'), and only a base-rig --prune removes the rows.

findings.title: The editor's own 'open' check of a client link is counted as the client opening it
findings.what: Every load of the public page increments view_count/last_viewed_at, including loads from the panel's own 'open' button. The panel presents the counter as whether the client has looked at the link.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor clicks 'open' to check the folder, then sends the link. The panel reads 'Opened 1 time, last today' and the editor believes the client has seen it when the client has not.

findings.title: The scheduler judges a computer by its LAST report however old it is, so a machine switched off weeks ago keeps a job schedulable/transient for ever
findings.what: fleet_facts reads every machine_state row with its stored capabilities (idle_seconds included) and has no reported_at bound. ranked_machines and explain therefore count a machine silent for a month as able, using its last idle answer. /jobs/machines computes `online`, but the scheduler never does.
findings.failure_scenario: A laptop last reported 2026-08-01 with ffmpeg and idle 900 s, then went into a drawer. The only live PC has somebody at it. explain says schedulable=true, reason '', and names the drawer laptop 'first choice', so Timeline Cards keeps waiting for ever. If its last report was not idle, the code is idle_wait/transient=true, and worst-answer-wins keeps it transient even when every live machine lacks the capability. For 60 s it can also win the rank grace against live machines.

findings.title: An editor's own requester-first download blocks that editor's queued searches while the server worker has nothing to do
findings.what: BUSY is defined as the phases a worker is inside and includes 'downloading'. A downloading job under a live local lease is hidden from the worker, but the queue's NOT EXISTS still counts it as the editor's busy job. The editor's next queued search, which only the server can run, waits for their own machine's download.
findings.failure_scenario: Sam's companion spends 40 minutes downloading 40 clips locally. His next search sits at queued (queued_behind 1, fleet_ahead 0) for the whole 40 minutes while the NAS worker idles. Probe: claim_next_job returns ann's job, then None, while sam's job B waits.

findings.title: The page never shows why the editor's computer gave a download back: handed_back_reason has no consumer, and claim refusals set no reason
findings.what: CR-171/CYT-11 gave the companion a sentence for each of the seven hand-backs 'so the page that has had its 202 learns WHY'. app.js never reads handed_back_reason, only polls the loopback while download_mode=='local', and treats a 202 as success. Claim refusals after the 202 (403 stale yt-dlp, 409 other computer, 410 skew/created on the server, attestation) call no hand_back, so they exist only in the companion log.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor presses DOWNLOAD and gets a 202. Their companion then finds under 5 GB free, an unmounted tree, or a refused claim. No toast appears. After a claim, the badge says 'downloading on your computer' with no progress for up to 180 s, then flips to the server. The clips stay on the NAS, where no lane brings them down, which is exactly the feedback the owner asked for on 2026-08-19.

findings.title: The download-terms toast sends the editor to a right-click menu item that no longer exists (CR-88) and ignores the companion's correct route
findings.what: The companion's refusal reason already carries 'Tray > Settings > Accept YouTube Terms'. The SPA drops it and shows a hardcoded 'right-click the tray icon, then Accept YouTube Terms'. The ten-item right-click menu has no such item. CR-145 fixed this in the companion copy but missed the browser.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor whose downloads fall back to the server looks in the right-click menu for the one fix they could make in ten seconds, cannot find it, and every download keeps landing only on the NAS.

findings.title: The collector's lease sweep ignores DASH_JOBS_COOLDOWN_SECONDS
findings.what: prune() calls expire_leases(conn, now, pin=pin) without the configured cooldown, so this common path always uses the 120 s default. Only the claim route passes settings.jobs_cooldown_seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets DASH_JOBS_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=0 so a sleeping laptop is not parked. The collector expires the laptop's lease and cools it down for 120 s anyway, and why shows 'cooling down until ...'.

findings.title: The why page says a lower-ranked machine is 'offered the job anyway once it has waited 60s' for forced, targeted and old jobs that have no grace
findings.what: The per-machine sentence always promises a 60 s wait. first_refusal gives forced and targeted jobs no grace, and a job past RANK_GRACE_SECONDS is already offered to every able machine.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin forces a proxy job and reads that the second machine will only be offered it after 60 s, then waits for something that has already happened.

findings.title: Documented key rotation signs the overlap release with the NEW key, and the REL-7 refusal tells the operator to override it
findings.what: Rotation step 1 says run `release_key.py new --force` + `bake --add`, then ship 'with the OLD key still signing'. But `new --force` moves the old key to release.key.superseded and writes the new key at release.key, which every signer reads. No doc names how to sign with the old key, and publish_latest has no --key option.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator follows step 1. REL-7 refuses and says an overlap release is the answer and to pass --allow-key-rotation 'if this is that deliberate step'. They pass it. Every machine on the current build refuses the build permanently. The feed channel is also re-signed with the new key, so every customer dashboard pinning the old key rejects the whole channel: fleet-wide stranding with no OTA recovery.

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. docs/RELEASE.md:675-678 tells the operator to run `release_key.py new --force` and `bake --add`, then ship "with the OLD key still signing". But cmd_new (tools/release_key.py:109-121) moves the old key to release.key.superseded and writes the new key at release.key. That default path is what every signer reads: key_path() in sign_release.py:414, publish_feed.write_channel:412 for the channel signature, the release.ps1:530 probe, and publish_latest.preflight:107. None of the rotation docs or refusal texts says how to keep signing with the old key. There is a workaround nobody mentions: CCSYNC_RELEASE_KEY pointed at release.key.superseded would work, because key_path() honours it and publish_latest's preflight only checks that release.key exists.

The gates do not catch it:
- release.ps1's baked-key check passes, because the new key is baked alongside the old one.
- The REL-7 check fires, but its message steers the operator the wrong way. publish_feed.py:1259-1262 says "`bake --add`, ship THAT (it trusts both keys) ... Pass --allow-key-rotation if this is that deliberate step". build_editor_package.ps1:460-462 says the same with -AllowKeyRotation. An operator who has just run bake --add is doing exactly that step, so they pass the flag. The correct overlap release should never need the override.

Result: the record is signed with a key that no machine on the current build trusts, so the fleet cannot take it. The channel is also re-signed with the new key, and dashboards verify the channel against DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS (release_feed.py:133/429/807). Any customer dashboard that pins only the old vendor key therefore rejects the whole feed.

Nothing in KNOWN_BUGS.md covers this; REL-7 is the guard that the misleading text defeats. Likelihood is low because rotation is rare and the refusal prints an all-caps warning. The impact is fleet-wide stranding with no over-the-air recovery, and the documented procedure leads straight to it, so high stands.

findings.title: Retracting the current build makes every policy=current site auto-publish a newer build the vendor only STAGED
findings.what: retract_record pops the current pointer without setting a replacement. A customer dashboard with no pointer for that pair falls back to the highest version on the channel, which can be a staged (never promoted) newer record.
findings.failure_scenario: The channel holds 0.9.77, 0.9.78 (current) and 0.9.79 (staged). The vendor retracts 0.9.78 to roll back. Every policy=current site now publishes 0.9.79 and makes it current once its soak passes. Probe: select_offered_records returns 0.9.78 before the retract and 0.9.79 after it, with pointer {}.

findings.title: Staged vendor records (and a pointer moved back) count as 'offered': invariant 11, the versions-behind alert and the HEALTH box cry wolf
findings.what: record_offer_state writes every companion version on the channel into feed_offered, and raises feed_publish_refused for any of them, ignoring the signed current pointer that _apply_policy uses. The readers downstream take the maximum as what the vendor offers.
findings.failure_scenario: The vendor publishes staged, or rolls back by moving the pointer backwards. Every customer dashboard then permanently reports 'the vendor offers X and this server has not published it' or 'published but not current', counts computers as behind, and shows behind_vendor. The next action it gives does not exist, although the server is behaving correctly.

findings.title: Dashboard auto-update ignores the channel's current pointer, so a STAGED dashboard bundle is applied at every policy=current site
findings.what: status() builds code_updates from every verified dashboard record, highest first, and _dashboard_auto_apply_reason applies code_updates[0] after the soak age. channel_current['dashboard/linux'] is never consulted, so a dashboard bundle cannot be staged, and a pointer moved back does not roll it back.
findings.failure_scenario: The vendor publishes dashboard 0.7.57 without --make-current (the RELEASE_PATHWAYS two-step), meaning to try it at the studio first. Every customer on policy=current applies it and restarts after soak_minutes.

findings.title: publish_latest's SYS-7 ordering gate judges a requires_dashboard that sign_release strips, and swallows the note that says so
findings.what: The gate reads the manifest's requires_dashboard, but publish_latest never enables kind extras, so the field is dropped from the signed record. sign_release's stderr NOTE is discarded on success. 0 of 99 records on this rig's last-published channel carry requires_dashboard.
findings.failure_scenario: The gate either refuses a publish over an ordering rule no customer enforces (compared against the dashboard bundle channel at 0.7.44, while dashboards move by image), or passes and leaves the operator believing customers are protected, while customer dashboards make the build current with no check.

findings.title: 'Re-run with --make-current when you are ready' is a no-op: the re-run skips the version as already published
findings.what: The already-published skip runs before --make-current is considered, so the advised re-run prints 'nothing to do' and never moves the pointer. RELEASE_PATHWAYS records the trap, but the tool still gives the advice.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator publishes staged, re-runs with --make-current as told, sees 'nothing to do' and a 'skipped' line, and assumes the build is live. policy=current customers keep being offered the previous build indefinitely.

findings.title: --allow-older is documented as the rollback, but publish_latest cannot roll the feed back and no tool moves the pointer alone

findings.title: A project name with an apostrophe breaks the ARCHIVE confirm, so the project archives with no question (a crafted folder name can run script)
findings.what: onsubmit="return window.confirm('Archive {{ p.label }}? ...')" puts the label into a JS single-quoted string. Jinja's ' is HTML-decoded back to ' before the handler compiles. p.label is the project's relative folder path (collector upsert_project), a name anyone with write access to the tree chooses.
findings.failure_scenario: A folder named "Editor's Cut" makes the handler a SyntaxError, so it is null and [ ARCHIVE ] submits with no confirm. A folder named x');fetch(...);(' runs script in the admin's session when they click ARCHIVE on that row.
findings.ledger: new (same shape as the fixed Cards entry at KNOWN_BUGS:29431)

verification.reason:
The mechanism holds. In dashboard/templates/admin_assignments.html:166, `{{ p.label }}` sits inside a single-quoted JS string in an `onsubmit` attribute. Jinja2Templates (ui.py:60) only HTML-autoescapes, so `'` becomes `'`. The browser decodes that back to `'` before it compiles the handler, so the escaping gives no protection in a JS-string context. I found no `|tojson` filter, no JS escaping and no Content-Security-Policy anywhere in src.

The label is attacker-influenced. `upsert_project` is called from collector.py:1020 and api.py:3546 with `rel` (the project's relative folder path on the NAS), and from collector.py:1257 with the Syncthing folder label, which the collector itself sets to `rel`. Folder names are not sanitised on the way in. A folder named "Editor's Cut" makes the handler a SyntaxError, so the attribute handler is null and the form submits with no confirm. A crafted name such as `x');fetch(...);('` runs as script in the admin's session.

Mitigations:
- The page is admin-only.
- The payload needs write access to the Projects tree.
- Archive is reversible.

Even so, stored XSS from a folder name into an admin session is a privilege escalation from anyone who can create a folder. KNOWN_BUGS.md has no open or fixed entry for it. It is the only template confirm that interpolates a value into a quoted JS string this way (grep of dashboard/templates). High stands.

findings.title: The fleet halt says it "releases itself 0s ago" for the whole time it is active
findings.what: halt.expires_at is in the future, and the `ago` filter clamps negative deltas to 0 and always adds 'ago'.
findings.failure_scenario: The every-page banner and the admin panel read 'it releases itself 0s ago' for the whole 24 h halt, i.e. already released. Proved: ui.ago(now+23h) == '0s ago'.

findings.failure_scenario: (a) A pasted SSH key or username disappears after 30 s. (b) A NAS CREATE takes up to 2 min. The poll puts back an idle [ CREATE ], the busy label vanishes, and the POST's notice or refusal is swapped into a detached box and never seen. The admin clicks CREATE again. The same happens on PUBLISH (downloads tens of MB) and CHECK NOW.
