findings.what: item.note is set only after the PUT resolves, and cfMove re-renders synchronously on the click that caused the blur, so the redrawn field shows the old caption.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor types a caption and immediately presses the up arrow on another row. The caption field goes back to empty although the server saved it, so the editor retypes it or concludes captions do not save.

findings.title: Two hamburgers and two gears in the b-roll header, meaning different things
findings.what: The injected dashboard topbar brings its nav-drawer menu button and its Settings gear. The b-roll row adds a second hamburger (U+2630), which opens client folders, and a second gear, which opens the b-roll share/tray panel.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor looking for client folders has no reason to press a hamburger icon. An admin who presses the lower gear expecting Settings gets a panel about ~/.broll-companion.json.

findings.title: The ingest Running list prints raw state tokens such as proxies_live
findings.what: The live panel prints item.state raw, while the expanded batch card uses ingestItemStateText (wire-1). The call site was missed.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor watching their own ingest reads 'proxies_live  Taipei/A001.mov', while the batch card shows the same clip as 'original still owed'.

findings.title: Ingest live controls offer Pause, Resume and Start now at once, whatever the state
findings.what: The buttons are disabled only when the batch is over, never toggled by state. The only confirmation is a toast carrying the companion's raw state token.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor cannot tell whether indexing is paused, presses Resume on a running batch, and gets 'CC Sync tray: running.' with no change on screen.

findings.title: Mode fallback toast says 'keyword' while the page switches to Hybrid
findings.what: applyModeAvailability sets state.mode='hybrid' and highlights Hybrid, but the toast reads 'Searching by keyword instead.'
findings.failure_scenario: Semantic search is unavailable. The editor reads 'keyword', sees Hybrid highlighted, and cannot tell which mode ran.

findings.title: Long error toasts vanish after 5 s, including the tray-unreachable self-test instructions
findings.what: Every toast lives a fixed 5000 ms with no dismiss control. The ~330-char tray-unreachable error, which includes a URL to open, cannot be read or copied in that time.
findings.failure_scenario: Append fails because Chrome blocked the local network. The editor loses the only instruction for telling 'tray down' apart from 'browser blocked' before finishing reading it.

findings.title: The b-roll SPA has no narrow layout: 718 px wide at a 390 px viewport
findings.what: The flag row is nowrap, the rail is a fixed 210 px, the cards are a fixed 240 px, and the detail layout's second column has a 260 px minimum.
findings.failure_scenario: On a phone the page scrolls sideways (docW=718 measured), and the grid gets about 170 px beside the rail, too narrow for a 240 px card.

findings.title: The YouTube page has no phone layout: its search row is 365 px wider than the screen
findings.where: ytdl/web/static/style.css:391 (.search-bar, no wrap; no @media rule in the file); ytdl/web/static/index.html:81-119
findings.what: .search-bar is a non-wrapping flex row of #q, #project (up to 320 px), #quality, the local switch, #period and #maxcand. None of them can shrink, and the stylesheet has no media query at all.
findings.failure_scenario: On a phone, headless Edge measured scrollWidth 847 against a 482 px viewport. Quality, the switch, the date filter, the candidate cap and GET LINKS sit off-screen, the shot/scope rows and review cards overflow, and the page scrolls sideways.

findings.title: Clicking a clip's title to watch it on YouTube also ticks or unticks it for download
findings.what: The title <a target=_blank> has no stopPropagation, so the click bubbles to the card's onclick, which calls toggle() and POSTs select.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor previews promising clips by clicking their titles. Each preview flips that clip's selection, and DOWNLOAD fetches a different set from the one they chose.

findings.title: The attestation lock on SEARCH / GET LINKS is undone by the project loader and by every submit
findings.what: setAttested(false) disables #go/#golinks, then loadProjects() sets disabled=false whenever projects exist, and the runSearch/runUrls finally blocks do the same. Accepting re-enables them over 'no projects ticked'. dataset.title is never set, so after accepting the tooltip still says 'Accept the download terms...'.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor who has not accepted sees SEARCH lit under the notice, presses it and gets a server 403 toast. An editor with no projects ticked who accepts gets an enabled SEARCH that the server then refuses.

findings.title: The music player pane is a fixed 150 px box that cuts off its own buttons and messages
findings.what: The content is not fixed: the action buttons wrap, and the no-waveform caption and the Resolve status/error line add rows. Anything past 150 px is clipped with no scroll.
findings.failure_scenario: A fleet track (no peaks) plus an 'import to bin' with no tray running measured 161 px of content at 1246 px wide (error line cut off) and 237 px on the phone layout (reveal/similar buttons and the message hidden).

findings.title: Rail filters, sort and '[ include them ]' silently throw away the typed search while the box still shows it
findings.what: Every rail control calls loadTracks() (browse) and never runSearch, while #q keeps the description. runSearch itself draws the '[ include them ]' button, which replaces the search results with an unranked browse list.
findings.failure_scenario: The editor searches 'tense driving synth pulse' and clicks '[ include them ]'. They get the whole library by filename under 'All tracks' with no match scores, and the search box still shows the query.
findings.ledger: related to MUSIC-4 (fixed in the other direction only)

findings.title: A length filter that matches nothing says 'The library is empty'
findings.what: The headline bits cover facet, axis and BPM only. The duration filter (and include-unknown) are not included, so the no-filters headline and empty-state sentence are chosen.
findings.failure_scenario: Secs min 900, apply: the list reads 'All tracks 0 tracks' and 'The library is empty. Drop some music in to get started.' on a 397-track library.

findings.title: One failed stats or facets call at load kills the whole music page, with a raw status line
findings.what: init awaits api/stats and api/facets before it wires any handler. A throw leaves nothing wired and prints 'Failed to load: api/stats -> 401' instead of failureText's session wording.
findings.failure_scenario: After a session expiry and a reload, SEARCH and ADD MUSIC do nothing, and the only text is a raw 401 line with no 'sign in again'.

findings.title: Music's sticky header is taller than the --header-h the rail parks under, and on a phone it takes a third of the screen
findings.what: The rail is sticky at a constant 134 px, but the header measured 150 px at 1246 px wide and 263 px at the phone layout, where it stays sticky.
findings.failure_scenario: On desktop the top 16 px of the rail (the FEEL heading) sits under the header while scrolling. On a 390x844 phone about a third of the screen is a frozen header.

findings.title: After a music batch finishes, the panel still says 'Running' and offers Run again on the same staged tracks
findings.what: mi.batchUid and mi.items are never cleared when a batch goes terminal. The live section keeps its 'Running' heading, and the staged, still-ticked tracks get an enabled Run button once mi.running goes false.
findings.failure_scenario: After 'all done', the editor sees 'Running' over 'all done' and the same 20 tracks with Run lit. Pressing it mints a second batch of the same files.

findings.title: YouTube's Recent searches list prints the raw phase enum that the progress strip translates
findings.what: Recent rows render j.phase raw (ready_for_review, terms_review, generating_terms), while the progress strip shows PHASE_LABEL words for the same job.
findings.failure_scenario: 'ready_for_review' in the list sits directly under 'READY FOR REVIEW' on the strip, and a parked terms_review job reads as an internal code.

findings.title: confirm_dialog never wraps its body, so the WIRED TO THE SERVER confirm is about 2,280 px wide with its buttons off-screen
findings.what: The body is a tk.Label with no wraplength, and the button bar is anchored to the right edge. A one-line paragraph body makes the window as wide as the paragraph.
findings.failure_scenario: The WIRED body (321 chars) measures 2,247 px in Consolas 10 on a 1,920 px screen, so CANCEL and OK are off-screen and only the X (cancel) is reachable. On a 1,366/1,536 px laptop the halt (1,582 px) and resume (1,442 px) confirms do the same.

findings.title: Nothing ticked is drawn as a red blocking line in Settings and pulls HELP to the top
findings.what: _lane_advisories tags _blocked_line as BLOCKING at the producer level, so the no_selection sentence (informational in tray.py) is styled 'warning' (red), and _help_first reorders the window as if something were wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: A laptop with nothing ticked shows 'No projects are ticked for this computer' in red, with HELP / COPY DIAGNOSTICS moved first. This breaks the owner rule that nothing ticked is never a warning on any surface. Probe: rank_advisories -> style='warning', _help_first -> ['HELP','SYNCING'].

findings.title: The licence dialog shows raw EULA.md, including the internal 'DRAFT FOR COUNSEL / TODO(legal)' comment
findings.what: _show_licence_dialog inserts bundled_text() verbatim. The file opens with an authoring HTML comment for the lawyer ('NOT YET EXECUTABLE', 'NOT been reviewed', 'Cablewrap Creative ... almost certainly NOT the correct contracting entity'), followed by the version marker and Markdown syntax.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer's editor on a new machine gets the NOT SYNCING licence modal. The first text they see says the agreement is unreviewed and not executable and names a retired brand, and they must click ACCEPT under it to sync.

findings.title: The Settings jump strip overflows the 720 px window, so ADVANCED is cut and HELP is invisible; Lines use a fixed wraplength of 660
findings.what: Section buttons go in one non-wrapping pack row at a fixed 720 px width. Label wraplength is fixed at 660 while the window can shrink to 560.
findings.failure_scenario: On a healthy machine the strip needs 841 px: ADVANCED ends at x=746 and HELP spans 754-815, so HELP cannot be seen. A narrowed window cuts off the right-hand ends of the red advisories.

findings.title: Settings says 'disconnected ... plug it back in' about a drive that is plugged in but not answering or mounted in the wrong place
findings.what: root_unfinished is set for every _root_absent state, but this Settings line hard-codes 'disconnected' instead of using drive_absent_phrase(root_state) or the site drive phrase.
findings.failure_scenario: A wedged SSD with 2 uploads owed: the tray and balloon say 'not answering ... restart this computer', while Settings says 'plug it back in', sending the editor to check a cable that is fine (SYNC-120).

findings.title: The local-stop release is 'Clear the sync stop' in the tray but the retired 'START SYNCING AGAIN' in Settings
findings.what: UX-19 renamed the tray row after its cause because the effect label is false while a pause is also set. The Settings button for the same action kept the old label.
findings.failure_scenario: With both a stop and a pause set, pressing START SYNCING AGAIN leaves the computer not syncing, and the halt confirm pointed the editor to a differently named control.

findings.title: The licence refusal in the tooltip is cut before its action; inside Settings it tells the reader to open Settings
findings.what: The tooltip hard-slices the blocked detail at 127 characters (head kept, the APP-4 anti-pattern), and the licence sentences are 129 and 149 characters. _licence_advisory's 'setup wizard' filter is dead since APP-9, so the Settings line still says 'Open Tray > Settings > READ AND ACCEPT THE LICENCE' right above that button.
findings.failure_scenario: After a EULA bump the tooltip ends '... Open Tray > Settings > READ A'. In the Settings window the editor is sent to the window they are already in.

findings.title: The fixer popup's 52-character destination combobox hides the default destination's last folder
findings.what: Every option carries the full project prefix, and the field and the popdown list are 52 characters wide, so the distinguishing tail is cut off.
findings.failure_scenario: The default 'Projects/2026/FF5/Civil Defence/B-roll/Editor Added/ruskin' (58 chars) loses the editor's folder, and deeper folders all look alike in the dropdown, so the editor chooses where FIX ALL files media by guesswork.

findings.title: The fixer popup's width is unbounded; with a long path the right-aligned FIX ALL bar goes off-screen
findings.what: The window's height is capped at 80% of the screen and its width is not. Path and clip-name Labels are unwrapped, and the button bar is sticky to the east edge.
findings.failure_scenario: A path of about 200+ characters on a 1,366 px laptop pushes FIX ALL / SKIP / LEAVE THIS FOLDER ALONE past the right edge of the screen.

findings.title: Fleet-jobs toggles: re-enabling omits the restart note, and the kind sentence is ungrammatical
findings.what: The re-enable balloon does not say the change takes effect at the next start, though every jobs_* key does. The kind balloon reads 'will no longer take transcribe audio (uses the graphics card) for the fleet'.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor re-enables fleet work, expects it to take effect now, and nothing changes until a restart.

findings.title: Muted text fails contrast (3.98:1), no neon_button shows keyboard focus, and confirm/notice dialogs have no keys
findings.what: MUTED #6f6f7a on BG is 3.98:1 and RED_DIM is 1.86:1; they are used for 8pt file paths, the 'dest:' label and every secondary button. neon_button sets highlightthickness=0. confirm_dialog and notice_dialog bind neither Escape nor Return and focus nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: The file path that identifies the out-of-tree clip is dim 8pt grey, and a keyboard-only user cannot see which button Space will press or dismiss a confirm without the mouse.

findings.title: Fixed 660x560 window clips CLOSE / BACK / log path off finish and install pages
findings.what: Every page packs its nav bar last (side=bottom), so when content exceeds 560 px Tk takes the space from the nav bar first. The finish page with warnings and the install page with the role-override note are both taller than the window.
findings.failure_scenario: Two ordinary capability misses (bootstrap's ~290-char device-ID text) squeeze CLOSE to 1 px; more warnings unmap the SSH-key field, 'Send these', the install-log path and CLOSE. On the install page with the role note BACK is unmapped (plain install page clips it to 16 px), leaving RETRY as the only visible action after a failure. Measured off-screen with Tk.

findings.title: Licence page shows raw draft EULA: TODO(legal) HTML comment, markdown, 14 em dashes
findings.what: eula_text() returns the .md verbatim into a Text widget. The first lines an editor reads are the internal 'DRAFT FOR COUNSEL ... NOT YET EXECUTABLE ... TODO(legal) ... almost certainly NOT the correct contracting entity' comment naming Cablewrap Creative, then # / ** markup, and 14 em dashes; test_no_em_dashes.py scans only *.py.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer's editor is asked to ACCEPT a document that says in its opening lines it is not executable and names the wrong (retired) entity.

findings.title: Interrupted-install page and close warning always claim 'no P drive', even for base installs and Macs; resume defaults to the editor radio
findings.what: Both texts are role/platform-blind although base cleanup never unmounts the drive (steps.py:2616, 2897) and a Mac has no drive letter. The breadcrumb records 'clean_slate:base' but show_interrupted ignores it and FINISH THE INSTALL returns to a role page defaulting to 'editor'.
findings.failure_scenario: A wired machine's interrupted install reopens saying the P drive is gone and nothing syncs (false), then preselects the remote-editor (destructive) radio; a Mac editor is told they have no P drive.
findings.ledger: new (radio default related to CR-66, deferred)

findings.title: winget Tailscale install: stale NOT INSTALLED, green on failure, and join check cannot find new tailscale.exe
findings.what: Install status is computed once at render; the winget worker ignores returncode and prints green success; tailscale_up on Windows tries only bare 'tailscale' against the wizard's PATH captured before Tailscale was installed, while tailscale_installed checks Program Files.
findings.failure_scenario: New editor clicks INSTALL TAILSCALE, signs in, CHECK CONNECTION keeps saying 'tailscale isn't joined yet' with NOT INSTALLED shown, until the wizard is restarted.

findings.title: Finish page copy contradicts itself and the install
findings.what: 'One more step: right-click the tray icon -> Sign in... is already done for you'; the SSH key was already POSTed by _offer_ssh_key but the page still says send it and never reports the result; truncation line points to 'COPY LOG on the previous page', unreachable (finish has no BACK, no COPY LOG).
findings.failure_scenario: Editor hunts for a step that does not exist and re-sends a key already in the admin's queue; with >6 warnings is sent to an unreachable button.

findings.title: Welcome says 'nothing else' is needed but next page requires dashboard URL
findings.what: Welcome text says only username/password are needed; the role page makes the dashboard URL REQUIRED (no default since WP0).
findings.failure_scenario: Editor starts with only their login as instructed and is blocked on page 2.

findings.title: Role-override note uses internal 'base'/'editor' instead of the radio labels
findings.what: Note says 'you picked base ... this is a editor install ... only the editor install unmaps P:', words that never appear on the role page, and offers only BEGIN INSTALL.
findings.failure_scenario: Non-admin editor on a wired machine cannot tell the install will disconnect their NAS drive (CR-66 destructive direction).

findings.title: No Enter key, no initial focus, no visible focus ring
findings.what: Sign-in has no <Return> binding, nothing takes focus on page open, neon_button uses highlightthickness=0.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor types password and presses Enter: nothing happens; tabbing shows no focus.

findings.title: Muted text 3.98:1 and field borders 1.86:1 contrast
findings.what: MUTED #6f6f7a on #0a0a0d is 3.98:1 at 8-9 pt, used for the REQUIRED dashboard-url label, radio subtitles explaining which install unmaps the drive, log path and BACK; RED_DIM field borders 1.86:1.
findings.failure_scenario: On a dim laptop the explanation of the destructive choice and the required field outline are hard to read.

findings.title: Wrong-account refusal says sign in as the already-signed-in account
findings.what: Message says 'Sign in as Y and run it again' when Y is already signed in; the cause is launching under another account via UAC credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor signs out/in as Y, relaunches the same way, gets the same refusal.

findings.title: Bootstrap end banner prints hand-run 'remaining manual steps' into wizard installs
findings.what: Every wizard run's log ends with 'tailscale up', 'generate an SSH keypair and send the .pub', 'see docs/EDITOR_SETUP.md', all already done by the wizard.
findings.failure_scenario: Editor/admin reading the install log generates or sends a second key.

findings.title: VERIFY & CONTINUE / CHECK CONNECTION not disabled while in flight
findings.what: No disabled state while the worker runs; a double click runs two verifications and each success calls show_install.
findings.failure_scenario: Double-click mints two identity tokens; if BEGIN INSTALL was pressed between results the second show_install replaces the live log widget mid-install.

findings.title: The fleet-halt alert sends the admin to a button and a page that do not exist
findings.what: The next action for _check_fleet_halt says 'SYNC STATUS, then [ RELEASE THE HALT ]'. No template has ever had that label. The real control is [ START SYNCING AGAIN ] / [ KEEP IT STOPPED ] on Settings, Users (/admin/users#admin-fleet-halt). The expired-halt alert also sends the admin to SYNC STATUS. The recovery wizard step says 'Put the fleet on hold' and links href=/fleet. The VOCABULARY_ALLOWED test entry still claims the label exists in the templates.
findings.failure_scenario: The fleet is halted over a weekend and the alert mail tells the owner to press [ RELEASE THE HALT ] on SYNC STATUS. There is no such button there, so syncing stays stopped for every editor until someone finds Settings, Users.

findings.title: 'Settings, Diagnostics' is not a page, and the notice links land on an empty div
findings.what: Five notice fix strings send the admin to 'Settings, Diagnostics', which is not in SETTINGS_NAV_GROUPS. The registry hrefs for server_error and collector_* point to /fleet#fleet-diagnostics, an empty div that fills only after clicking [ READ THE ANSWER ] on a computer that has uploaded a bundle.
findings.failure_scenario: The collector keeps failing. The owner clicks the notice, lands on SYNC STATUS scrolled to nothing, and finds no Diagnostics entry in Settings, so there is nothing to send and no next step.

findings.title: More next-action sentences name buttons or pages by names they do not have
findings.what: The alerts say [ ASK WHY ], but the button is [ ASK THIS COMPUTER WHY ]. They say [ UPDATE THE DASHBOARD ], but the button is [ UPDATE NOW ] in the [ DASHBOARD ] panel. They say 'Settings, Projects', but there is no such page, and /project-setup is not linked from the dashboard.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner following the mail or notice looks for a button or page that does not exist under that name.

findings.title: Companion copy outside the vocabulary scan still says 'machine', 'lane B' and 'parked' to editors and admins
findings.what: These modules are not in the companion scan's MODULES tuple, but their strings reach people. The ytdl REASON_* strings are printed verbatim in the ytdl page toast (next to 'this computer'). File-move details show as 'lane B had already moved this folder on this machine' on the project page MOVES history. The proxy tray balloon says 'This machine has no ffmpeg'. The Resolve undo result begins 'Parked:'. The Cards refusal 'the fleet is halted... (CR-68)' shows in a fleet grid tooltip.
findings.failure_scenario: An editor sees 'this machine' and 'this computer' in one toast. An admin reads 'lane B' and a bug id, both retired terms, on dashboard pages.

findings.title: The companion and the dashboard give two different routes to Copy diagnostics
findings.what: The companion constant says 'Tray > Settings > COPY DIAGNOSTICS FOR YOUR ADMIN' (no Help step). The dashboard constant says 'Settings > Help > Copy diagnostics'. The real button is labelled 'COPY DIAGNOSTICS FOR YOUR ADMIN'. fleet_grid.html:472 hand-writes a third spelling.
findings.failure_scenario: The admin and the editor are given two different directions to the same button, which is the drift the one-constant rule was meant to prevent.

findings.title: The ' -- ' stand-in em dash is banned in templates but ships in dashboard Python copy
findings.what: The DUI-14 scan covers templates only. About 70 Python literals rendered into pages or HTTP details contain ' -- '. Examples: the login page error 'the server is busy checking sign-ins -- try again' and the halt refusal 'say why -- every editor's tray will show this'.
findings.failure_scenario: Editors and admins see the banned typewriter em dash on the login page and the Users page.

findings.title: 'Sign in' everywhere except the topbar's [ LOGIN ] / [ LOGOUT ] / [ LOGOUT ALL ]
findings.what: The login page, the tray and the SPAs say sign in / sign out. The topbar buttons say LOGIN / LOGOUT / LOGOUT ALL, and the LOGOUT ALL confirm mixes 'Sign yourself out' with 'log in again'.
findings.failure_scenario: One action has two names, sometimes in the same dialog, and a non-technical owner has to guess that they are the same thing.
